option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: After returning from South Africa in January 1915, Gandhiji carried out his first successful Satyagraha in Bihar’s Champaran district in 1917. In 1916, a Champaran farmer, Rajkumar Shukla, met Gandhiji in Lucknow and urged him to visit Champaran. The Champaran issue was quite old. By the end of the 19th century, German synthetic dyes replaced indigo in the market. As a result, the European plantation owners in Champaran were forced to stop indigo cultivation. The peasants too wanted to get rid of indigo cultivation as a cash crop. Taking advantage of the peasants helplessness, the white planters arbitrarily increased rent and other illegal taxes in the name of releasing them from their contracts. It was against this exploitation of the peasants that Gandhiji began the Champaran Satyagraha.

explanation: Madam Cama was born on 24 September 1861. Her parents were Parsis. Sorabji Framji Patel was her father. She married Rustam K. R. Cama, who was a lawyer and a social worker. Madam Cama served as the private secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji, a great pioneer leader of India’s national movement. Later, after coming in contact with some patriotic students and European intellectuals, she joined the freedom movement. She participated in the International Socialist Conference held at Stuttgart, Germany, on 22 August 1907. In this very conference, she unfurled the Indian tricolour flag. She was the first person to hoist the Indian flag on foreign soil or on an international platform. The flag hoisted there was a modified form of the Calcutta Flag. She is called the ‘Mother of the Indian Revolution’.

explanation: On 31 December 1922, in a meeting held at the residence of the Maharaja of Tikari in Gaya, the formation of a new party within the Congress—‘Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party’ was announced. In 1923, the ‘Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party’ (Swaraj Party) was formed, and from 20–22 February 1923, the general meeting of this newly formed party was held in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). In this meeting, the party’s programme and constitution were approved and the party was given the new name ‘Swaraj Party’. C. R. Das became its President and Motilal Nehru became its General Secretary. This party was formed with the objective of contesting council elections while remaining within the Congress. It also participated in the elections to the State Councils as well as the Central Legislative Council and achieved good success. Their real aim was to enter these assemblies, present their views, and practise non-cooperation with the government from within. The Swaraj Party was established after the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

On 22 May, 1930, a clash took place between the I. R.A. members and the army, in which 80 soldiers and 12 revolutionaries were killed. Surya Sen was arrested on 16 February, 1933. He was tried and was hanged on 12 January, 1934.

question: Soap removes grease by
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Emulsification is the process of mixing two or more immiscible liquids to form a semi-stable mixture. Soap molecules are generally long-chain compounds with polar groups; for example, soap (fatty salts of sodium and potassium). A soap molecule has two parts- (i) a long hydrocarbon chain (C17H35) which is soluble in fat, and (ii) a water-soluble polar part (–COO– Na+ group). During emulsification, the non-polar alkyl part (C17H35) dissolves oil or grease, while the polar part (–COO– Na+) dissolves in water. When rubbed properly, grease becomes suspended in water as tiny droplets and is easily washed away with running water.

He made Gulbarga the capital of his newly established empire and named it “Ahsanabad.” For administering the empire, he divided it into four tarafs (provinces)—Gulbarga, Daulatabad, Berar, and Bidar. Each province was under a governor. The Gulbarga province was the most important, and Bijapur was also included in it. He fought the Hindu rulers of the south and adopted the practice of granting posts and jagirs to his followers. He ordered that jizya should not be collected from Hindus.

explanation: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only after the Appropriation Bill is passed. However, if there is a change in the government at the end of the financial year and the new government does not immediately introduce the Appropriation Bill, or if for any other reason money is needed even before the Appropriation Bill is passed, then under Article 116(1)(a) the Lok Sabha can pass a Vote on Account and approve an advance amount for the government. Article 116 also provides that if, in emergency circumstances, the government needs a very large amount of money—such as during war—then the Lok Sabha grants a Vote of Credit, and Parliament authorizes the withdrawal by law.

subject: Polity
question: What is the nature of the Indian Constitution?
option_d: Federal in nature but unitary in spirit
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: Federal in nature but unitary in spirit
explanation: Constitutional experts generally classify constitutions into two main types—(i) Federal and (ii) Unitary. A unitary constitution is one in which all powers are vested in a single government, usually the central government. In such a system, provinces/states remain subordinate to the centre. In contrast, a federal constitution divides powers between the Centre and the States, and both governments function independently within their respective spheres. There has been considerable difference of opinion among jurists regarding the nature of the Indian Constitution. According to the Constitution-makers, it is federal; however, Prof. Jennings objected to calling it fully federal. Prof. K. C. Wheare described it as a quasi-federal constitution, or as a unitary constitution with federal features playing a supporting role. Jennings also pointed out a strong tendency towards centralization in the Indian Constitution. Therefore, from the above analysis, we can say that the Indian Constitution is neither purely federal nor purely unitary; rather, it is federal in structure but unitary in spirit.

subject: Ancient History
question: What is the most significant feature of the Indus Valley Civilization?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The main feature of the Indus Valley Civilization is considered to be town planning. Here, cities and towns were established according to a fixed plan. Among the buildings made of burnt bricks, the Great Bath and the Granary of Mohenjodaro. Their surfaces were made of burnt bricks and were joined with gypsum. Buildings made of burnt bricks, planned architecture, and advanced trade and commerce were the major characteristics of this civilization. It is noteworthy that, unlike ancient civilizations such as Mesopotamia and Egypt, clear evidence of places of worship is not found in the Harappan Civilization. Similarly, the first true arch in India is seen in Balban’s tomb. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

subject: Ancient History

option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the royal court of Chandragupta Maurya. Earlier, he had served as Seleucus’s envoy in the royal court of the satrap of Arachosia.

subject: Ancient History
question: Kautilya's Arthashastra is a book on
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Arthashastra by Kautilya (Chanakya) deals comprehensively with the political and administration of the state, including economic policy, foreign policy, law, statecraft, military strategy, and wealth. The Saptang Theory in Arthashastra describes seven wings of administration. Because it covers all the options (B, C, D), the answer is E (more than one of the above).

subject: Ancient History
question: Tripitakas are the sacred books of the
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Tripitaka is the most important among Buddhist scriptures. After Buddha’s death, his teachings were compiled and divided into three parts; these are collectively called the Tripitaka. These are— 1. Vinaya Pitaka (rules related to the Sangha and a collection of conduct related to daily life), 2. Sutta Pitaka (a collection of sermons delivered by Gautama Buddha and his chief disciples), and 3. Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical doctrines of Buddhism).

subject: Ancient History
question: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Ashoka’s Dhamma (Dharma) was a moral code. Through his second and seventh pillar edicts, Ashoka conveys the message—“Apasinave bahukayane daya dane, sache sochaye madave sadhave cha.” That is, do less wrongdoing, do welfare, show compassion and charity, speak the truth, live with purity, maintain gentleness in nature, and uphold goodness. Thus, the basic message of Ashoka’s Dhamma includes peace and nonviolence, respect for elders, and religious tolerance. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

subject: Ancient History
question: The division of Mauryan society into seven classes is particularly mentioned in
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above

subject: Ancient History
question: The famous Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Fa-Hien was a Chinese traveler, and he visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II. He wrote a detailed account of the life of the people here. In his account, he did not mention the king’s name. The Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Emperor Harsha. He described the multi-storeyed bronze monastery built by Harsha at Nalanda. In his account, he mentioned that during Harsha’s period the Shudras practiced agriculture. He also mentioned the assembly held at Prayagraj (Prayag) in his travelogue. Therefore, both statement (1) and statement (2) are incorrect.

subject: Medieval
question: The Chola age was most famous for
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The most notable feature of Chola rule is seen in the functioning of autonomous village institutions. In fact, during this period, villages were complete units of local selfgovernment, and village administration was carried out by the villagers themselves.

subject: Medieval
question: The mighty gateways found at the temples of South India are called
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The mighty gateways found at the temples of South India are called Gopurams. The Dravidian style fl ourished during the Pandyas and Cholas. In the Pandya period, the temples were small, but many ramparts were built around their courtyard. Their gateways, which were called Gopurams; were grand, spacious and richly ornamented with craftsmanship. The speciality of Chola period architecture is not the temple, but the Gopuram.

subject: Medieval
question: The remains of Vijayanagara empire are found in
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The ruins of Hampi (situated in Central Karnataka) represent the ancient capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. The Virupaksha temple, located in Hampi, was built during the Vijayanagara period. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

subject: Medieval
question: Who was the first Muslim ruler to formulate the 'theory of kingship' similar to the 'theory of divine right of the kings'?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Balban was the first Muslim ruler who propounded the theory of kingship on the lines of the theory of divine right of kings. According to this, the Sultan is the representative of God on earth (niyabat-e-khudai), and his position comes after the Prophet. The king is zill-e-Allah or zill-e-ilahi, i. e., the reflection of God. He said to his son Bughra Khan—“The office of the Sultan is the living symbol of absolutism.”

subject: Medieval
question: Paper came to be used in India in the
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The first use of paper in India may be considered to have begun approximately during the 7th to 8th centuries. According to available evidence, by the 11th century, documents written on paper began to appear in India, and in the 12th–13th centuries, the use of paper is clearly seen in manuscripts and royal records. In its final answer key, the Bihar Public Service Commission has selected option (B) as the correct option.

subject: Medieval

option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above

The development of painting began during Humayun’s reign. In Akbar’s reign, European painting influenced the Mughal painting style. In Akbar’s court, Miskin was a painter of the European style. During Akbar’s time, Daswanth was a leading painter. Jahangir’s reign is called the Golden Age (Golden Period) of Mughal painting.

These structures are sometimes described as the 'powerhouses of the cell' as they generate energy through respiration. During cellular respiration, the initial process takes place in cytoplasm and then in mitochondria.

The Finance Commission also recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India. It submits its report to the President. question: The Indigo Rebellion was about
option_a: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced to
option_b: the peasant wanting to grow indigo but being forced not to
option_c: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced to grow at a price that was unacceptable
option_d: a protest movement that carried an indigo-coloured flag
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced to grow at a price that was unacceptable
explanation: The Indigo Revolt began from Govindpur village in Nadia district of Bengal. Under the leadership of two former employees of an indigo planter—Digambar Biswas and Vishnu Biswas (Vishnucharan Biswas)—the peasants united there and stopped cultivating indigo. This was the most widespread and militant revolt in the history of indigo movements in terms of demands. The Indigo Revolt of Bengal was the peasants’ direct struggle against exploitation. The cultivators of Bengal who wanted to grow rice in their fields were forced by European indigo planters to cultivate indigo. Those who refused indigo cultivation had to face the oppressive machinery of the planters. In March 1859, thousands of raiyats in Bengal refused to cultivate indigo. As the revolt spread, the raiyats also refused to pay rent to the planters. By 1860, the indigo movement spread to Nadia, Pabna, Khulna, Dhaka, Malda, Dinajpur, etc. Due to the unity of the peasants, by 1860 almost all indigo factories in Bengal were closed. The intellectual class of Bengal expressed support for this revolt through newspaper articles and public meetings. The editor of “Hindu Patriot,” Harishchandra Mukherjee, played a special role in it. The atrocities of indigo planters were vividly portrayed by Dinabandhu Mitra in his play “Neel Darpan.”

explanation: On the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935, provincial legislature elections were held in February, 1937. In July 1937, the Congress formed ministries in six provinces—Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces and Berar, Odisha, Bihar and the United Provinces. Later, Congress also formed ministries with allied parties in the North-West Frontier Province and Assam. In the 1936–37 elections, the release of political prisoners was one of the major issues for Congress. Congress governments in various provinces tried to release political prisoners, but the Governors opposed these efforts. As a result, the elected Congress governments of the United Provinces and Bihar resigned on 15 February, 1938.

question: Who established Asht Pradhan?

explanation: Ashta Pradhan literally means a council of ministers. It was a system of ministerial delegation in the Maratha empire. Chhatrapati Shivaji formalized the institution of a council of eight ministers on the occasion of his coronation in 1674 at the fort of Raigad. The council included: Peshwa (Finance and general administration), Majumdar/Amatya (Revenue and Finance minister), Waqenavis/Mantri (Home Minister), Dabir/Sumant (Foreign Minister), Surnavis/Sachiv (Head of Royal correspondence), Pandit Rao/Sadar (Head of religious affairs), Sar-i-Naubat/Senapati (Military commander), and Nyayadhish (Justice).

subject: Medieval
question: Which Delhi Sultan built maximum number of canals?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The reign of Firuz Tughluq is famous for building the biggest network of canals for irrigation purpose. They were:- (1) Sutlej river to Ghaggar (96 miles) (2) Yamuna river to Hisar (150 miles), (3) Hill of Sirmor to Hansi, (4) Ghaggar river to Firozabad and (5) Yamuna river to Firozabad. He also engraved 150 wells for irrigation and betterment of passengers. According to Firista, Firuz built 50 dams and 30 lakes at diff erent places. Firuz Shah was the fi rst Sultan of Delhi who imposed ‘Haqq-i-Sharb’ tax on irrigation. Those farmers who used to irrigate their fi elds from the water of the royal canal had to give 1/10th part of the produce to the government.

subject: Modern History
question: Under whose leadership was suppression of Thugs achieved?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The British government believed that Thugs included followers of both Hindu and Muslim faiths; however, in reality, these people worshipped Kali, Durga or Bhavani and usually killed their victims as a sacrifice to the goddess. The Thugs believed that this occupation was ordained by fate, and that a person’s death was written in destiny in the same way. There were some differences of opinion on the issue of Sati, but thugs the entire public supported the government. Lord William Bentinck appointed Captain William Henry Sleeman to take action against the Thugs. He captured about 1,562 Thugs (between 1826 and 1835). Many Thugs were hanged, and the rest were transported for life. After 1837, organized Thuggee came to an end.

question: In 1930, from where Mahatma Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience Movement?

explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started his famous Dandi March accompanied by his trusted volunteers from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930 A. D. The march was over 241 miles, from Gandhi’s ashram in Sabarmati to Gujarat's coastal village of Dandi. The volunteers walked for 24 days. On April 5, 1930 A. D. he reached Dandi and on 6 April he violated the salt law, manufacturing salt by boiling seawater. This marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement. This Movement spread all over India under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. A leader like C. Rajagopalachari took up Salt March in Tamil Nadu from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam. Note: Bihar Public Service Commission has marked option (d) as correct answer in its fi nal answer key, which seems incorrect.

explanation: After 1928, Bardoli (in Surat district of Gujarat) became a centre of political activities. The ‘Mehta brothers’ of Bardoli (Kalyanji and Kunvarji) and Dayalji Desai started an agitation in support of the peasants from 1928. Later, it was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Under Patel’s leadership, the ‘No-Tax (Sarabandi)’ movement was launched in 1928. It is noteworthy that during the Non-Cooperation Movement, Gandhiji had planned to launch a no-tax (Sarabandi) movement from Bardoli in 1922, but due to the Chauri- Chaura incident, this plan was postponed. The Bihar Public Service Commission has mistakenly written the year of the Sarabandi (no-tax) movement as 1922 instead of 1928, which is incorrect.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who led the 1857 Revolt in Bihar?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: In 1857, the revolt at Jagdishpur was led by Kunwar Singh, who belonged to Arrah (Bhojpur district) in Bihar. He raised the banner of revolt against the British. Nature had endowed him with indomitable courage, bravery, and the ideal qualities of a military leader; therefore, he is rightly regarded as the “Lion of Bihar” during the revolt. He overthrew British authority in the then Shahabad and established his own government. He moved towards Kalpi to help Nana Saheb for a joint attack on Kanpur. He carried the flame of revolt to Rohtas, Mirzapur, Rewa, Banda and Lucknow, where he was welcomed with great respect. As his final success, he badly defeated the British near his hometown Jagdishpur. During this battle, he was severely injured after being defeated by the British commander William Taylor, and he attained martyrdom on 26 April, 1858. However, in some sources the date of his death is given as 9 May, 1858, which is erroneous.

Shudraka was a Gupta-period playwright. Saumila is a Gupta-period playwright, whom Kalidasa mentions along with Bhasa and Kaviputra. Thus, in the Gupta period, none of the above worked in the field of medicine. However, the Bihar Public Service Commission, in both its preliminary and final answer keys, considered option (a) as the correct answer. Since the Gupta period begins from 275 AD (Sri Gupta), which is about 1000 years after the accepted period of Sushruta (about 1000 BC to 600 BC), it is not reasonable to consider Sushruta as a contemporary of the Gupta period.

In the Mughal style, while painting human figures, it was common that in the same painting different painters painted the face, the body and the legs. Jahangir claimed that he could identify the separate contributions of different painters in any painting. Besides painting hunting, war and royal court scenes, there was special progress during Jahangir’s reign in the art of painting humans and animals. Abul Hasan made a painting of Jahangir’s coronation, which was placed on the main page of Jahangir’s autobiography Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri. Jahangir’s period is called the Golden Age of Mughal painting.

subject: Polity
question: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding parliamentary form of Government?
option_a: The Legislature is responsible to Judiciary.
option_b: The Legislature is responsible to Executive.
option_c: The Legislature and the Executive are independent.
option_d: The President is responsible to Judiciary.
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: In general, there are two systems of government— parliamentary and presidential. India, following Great Britain, has adopted the parliamentary system. In a parliamentary system, members of the legislature form the executive, and the executive is responsible to the legislature. The executive is controlled by the legislature, and the judiciary can conduct judicial review of the actions of both the executive and the legislature. The President is not responsible to the judiciary. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following was constituted under the Panchayati Raj system?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Panchayati Raj is a system of democratic decentralization. Provisions related to Panchayats are mentioned in Part IX of the Constitution under Articles 243 to 243-O. In 1957, the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee presented a plan of democratic decentralization and recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. Under this system, there is a Gram Panchayat at the village level, a Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and a Zila Parishad at the district level. Accepting these recommendations, the Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated at Nagaur on 2 October 1959 by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru. It is noteworthy that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. Therefore, the correct option is (c).

subject: Polity
question: Who amongst the following is a land record officer?

explanation: Patwari is the land record officer at Subdivision or tehsil level. He is a link between the village and the government, the lowest state functionary in the revenue collection system, and maintains the record of ownership and tilling.

subject: Polity
question: Which one of the following characteristics is not true for unitary form of Government?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Major features of a unitary form of government include centralisation of power, quick decision-making, a flexible constitution, a single judiciary, uniformity of law throughout the territory, single citizenship, provisions for emergency, etc. However, it is not necessary that such a system is ideal for large countries. In large countries, a federal system may also work better. Therefore, the expected answer is option (c).

subject: Polity
question: What is the objective of Community Development Programmes?

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The word “virus” is derived from the Latin word “virus”, which literally means poison or sticky liquid. Viruses are acellular, ultramicroscopic organisms that can multiply only inside a living cell. Generally, enzymes are absent in viruses; however, some viruses such as retroviruses contain certain enzymes. Chemically, a virus is a segment of nucleic acid surrounded by a protein coat. Outside the host cell, viruses can neither perform any biological activity nor replicate. Enzymes are also present in lichen, bacteria, and algae.

Due to iodine deficiency in the body, goitre occurs.

explanation: For the development of treatment for Parkinson’s disease, the Swedish neuroscientist Arvid Carlsson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in the year 2000. His research showed that Parkinson’s disease occurs due to a deficiency of dopamine in certain parts of the brain, and an effective medicine (L-dopa) can be developed for it.

When iodine and thyroxine levels in the blood decrease, secretion of TSH from the pituitary increases. Its effect is to stimulate the thyroid to secrete more and more hormones. Due to iodine deficiency in the body, a disease called goitre occurs.

subject: Modern History
question: Who among the following participated in the Parliament of Religions held at Chicago in 1893?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 in memory of his guru. After taking sannyasa, he made an extensive study of religious scriptures. The credit for giving a practical form to the interpretation of his guru’s teachings goes to Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902). He described these teachings in simple language. Swami Vivekananda emerged as a propagator of this Neo-Hinduism. In 1893, he went to Chicago, where he delivered his famous speech at the ‘Parliament of the World’s Religions’ (World Parliament of Religions). Through this speech, for the first time, he presented the importance of India’s culture before the Western world in a very effective manner. After this, he travelled in America and England and propagated Hinduism. Swamiji strongly condemned the tendency in Hinduism that says, “Don’t touchism.” According to him, Hinduism had now become confined only to food and drink. He was very unhappy with religion’s silence on the exploitation of the poor by the rich. According to him, to speak of religion to a hungry person is an insult to God and humanity. Vivekananda did not give any political message; yet, through his writings and speeches, he awakened in the new generation a renewed sense of self-respect in their past. He was a true patriot. Subhas Chandra Bose said about him: “As far as Bengal is concerned, we may look upon Vivekananda as the ‘Spiritual Father’ of the modern national movement.”

In 1923, the ‘Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party’ (Swaraj Party) was formed, and from 20–22 February 1923, the general meeting of this newly formed party was held in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). In this meeting, the party’s programme and constitution were approved and the party was given the new name ‘Swaraj Party’. C. R. Das became its President and Motilal Nehru became its General Secretary. This party was formed with the objective of contesting council elections while remaining within the Congress. It also participated in the elections to the State Councils as well as the Central Legislative Council and achieved good success. Their real aim was to enter these assemblies, present their views, and practise non-cooperation with the government from within. The Swaraj Party was established after the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

explanation: In 1857, the revolt at Jagdishpur was led by Kunwar Singh, who belonged to Arrah (Bhojpur district) in Bihar. He raised the banner of revolt against the British. Nature had endowed him with indomitable courage, bravery, and the ideal qualities of a military leader; therefore, he is rightly regarded as the “Lion of Bihar” during the revolt. He overthrew British authority in the then Shahabad and established his own government. He moved towards Kalpi to help Nana Saheb for a joint attack on Kanpur. He carried the flame of revolt to Rohtas, Mirzapur, Rewa, Banda and Lucknow, where he was welcomed with great respect. As his final success, he badly defeated the British near his hometown Jagdishpur. During this battle, he was severely injured after being defeated by the British commander William Taylor, and he attained martyrdom on 26 April, 1858. However, in some sources the date of his death is given as 9 May, 1858, which is erroneous.

explanation: After returning from South Africa in January 1915, Gandhiji carried out his first successful Satyagraha in Bihar’s Champaran district in 1917. In 1916, a Champaran farmer, Rajkumar Shukla, met Gandhiji in Lucknow and urged him to visit Champaran. The Champaran issue was quite old. By the end of the 19th century, German synthetic dyes replaced indigo in the market. As a result, the European plantation owners in Champaran were forced to stop indigo cultivation. The peasants too wanted to get rid of indigo cultivation as a cash crop. Taking advantage of the peasants helplessness, the white planters arbitrarily increased rent and other illegal taxes in the name of releasing them from their contracts. It was against this exploitation of the peasants that Gandhiji began the Champaran Satyagraha.

explanation: The Champaran Movement (1917) was Gandhiji’s first Satyagraha movement in India, in which he used civil disobedience. In protest against this announcement, a historic meeting was held at the Calcutta Town Hall, where the formal declaration was made of the Swadeshi Movement. When the Partition of Bengal was implemented in October 1905, that day was observed as a “Day of Mourning”. On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore, it was also observed as “Rakhi Day”. Nationalists observed this day to demonstrate the unbroken unity of Bengal. On the lines of Tagore’s Shantiniketan, the Bengal National College was established. Very soon, many national schools were set up across the country. In March 1906, the National Council of Education was formed. The Swadeshi Movement raised the slogan of self-reliance and self-power. The question of self-support and self-reliance was linked with national self-respect, honour, and self-confidence. The Congress, in its Calcutta Session (1906), also passed four resolutions related to the Swadeshi Movement, the Boycott Movement, National Education, and Self-government. Thus, it is clear that in opposition to the Partition of Bengal, nationalists launched movements such as Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, and Self-government.

Under it, the President has the power to summon each House of Parliament from time to time; however, the session of Parliament must be summoned in such a manner that the interval between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session is not more than six months. In other words, at least two sessions of Parliament must be held in a year. Generally, in India, three sessions of the Lok Sabha are held in a year— 1. Budget Session (February–May) 2. question: If 'One Nation One Election' is to be realized in India, which Article of the Indian Constitution will require an amendment?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: If the system of “One Nation, One Election” is implemented in India, then it will be necessary to align the tenure of all State Legislative Assemblies with the tenure of the Lok Sabha. In such a situation, the tenure of State Assemblies will have to be increased or reduced accordingly, and the existing tenure of the Lok Sabha will also have to be adjusted in the same manner. Further, after implementing this system, suitable provisions will also have to be made for situations where the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies are dissolved prematurely. Therefore, for such a system, amendments would be required in Article 83 (Duration of the Houses of Parliament), Article 85 (Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution), Article 172 (Duration of State Legislatures), Article 174 (Sessions of the State Legislature, prorogation and dissolution), Article 356 (Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States/President’s Rule in States), etc. It is noteworthy that a high-level committee on “One Nation, One Election” was constituted on 2 September 2023 under the chairmanship of former President Ram Nath Kovind, which submitted its report to President Droupadi Murmu on 14 March 2024.

explanation: Ikhtiyar al-Din Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji (Ibn Bakhtiyar Khalji) was the real founder of Turkish power in Bihar.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who was the first Indian Governor of Bihar?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha was born on 24 March, 1863, at Raipur in Birbhum, Bengal. He was the first Indian to be appointed Advocate General of Bengal in 1905. His appointment to this post was confirmed in 1908. In 1920, he was appointed Governor of Bihar and Orissa, and he was the first Indian to obtain this post in administration. Due to health reasons, he resigned from his post in 1921. He died on 4 March, 1928.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who were the leaders of Santhal Revolt?
option_a: Gaurakshni Bhagat and Keshav Chandra Roy
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: In 1855-56 A. D., Sidhu (Sido), Kanhu (Kanu), Chand and Bhairav the four brothers, gave a call for rebellion. The rebellious Santhals assembled and raised their arms against the British revenue system.

subject: Bihar Special
question: In which year the Chauri Revolt of Bihar took place?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The revolt was led by Chaurs (meaning looters) in the year 1798 in Bihar. Also known as Jungle Mahal movement, started in the Chotanagpur area of Bengal presidency. The Chuar Mutiny, led by Durjan Singh, was at its height in 1798-99.

subject: Bihar Special
question: In which year was Orissa separated from Bihar?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: On 1st April 1936, Orissa was separated from Bihar under the Government of India Act, 1935. Bihar was separated from Bengal in 1912 (Bihar Diwas: 22nd March). Jharkhand was carved out in 2000 by Bihar Reorganization Act.

subject: Ancient History
question: Where was the first Buddhist Council convened?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held immediately after the death of Buddha in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha (Rajgir). At that time, Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha. This council was presided over by Mahakassapa (Mahakashyapa), and Buddha’s chief disciples Ananda and Upali were also present. In it, Buddha’s teachings were compiled and divided into two Pitakas—Sutta and Vinaya. Ananda and Upali were considered the authorities on Dhamma and Vinaya respectively.

subject: Ancient History
question: Which Gupta ruler assumed the throne after killing his elder brother?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: After Samudragupta, his son Ramagupta became the ruler. However, since he could not effectively resist the Shaka invasions, his brother Chandragupta II killed Ramagupta, married his wife Dhruvadevi, and achieved victory over the Shakas.

subject: Medieval
question: Who laid the foundation of Vardhana dynasty?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: According to Banbhatt's composition Harshcharita the establishment of Vardhan dynasty was done by a person named Pushyabhuti, in Thaneshwar/Sthaneshwar. Harshvardhan was the greatest ruler of this dynasty.

subject: Ancient History
question: Who established trade relations with Roman empire?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: India’s trade with the Roman Empire began during the Sangam period with the Chera state. Many Roman objects have been found from Arikamedu.

subject: Medieval
question: The Muslim ruler whose empire was regarded as a part of Dar-ul-Islam was
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: During the reign of Iltutmish, in 1229 AD, the Caliph of Baghdad bestowed a robe of honour (khilat) upon him. Now the Sultanate, in theory, became a part of Dar-ul-Islam under the Caliph of Baghdad.

subject: Medieval
question: Who among the following opposed the power of the Khalifa?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: None of the sultans given in the options opposed the power of the Khalifa. Iltutmish obtained recognition from the Khalifa; however, the Sultan of Bengal, Ghiyasuddin, had also obtained recognition from the Khalifa. By attacking him, Iltutmish, in a way, also challenged the authority of the Khalifa. Alauddin Khilji, Balban, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq were all practically independent rulers, but none of them opposed the power or authority of the Khalifa. Only Mubarak Khilji declared himself the Khalifa and assumed the title Khalifatullah. In this way, he opposed the authority of the Khalifa.

subject: Medieval
question: Tughril Khan raised a standard of revolt during whose reign?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: An important revolt during Balban’s reign was the revolt of Tughril Khan. Balban had appointed Tughril Khan as the governor of Bengal, but he declared himself the independent ruler of Bengal, assumed the title of “Sultan Mugisuddin,” issued coins in his own name, and also had the khutba read in his name. To suppress Tughril’s revolt, Balban first sent an army under Amin Khan and thereafter under Bahadur, but both failed. Enraged, Balban advanced towards Bengal along with his son Bughra Khan, but Tughril fled after abandoning his capital. Ultimately, Tughril was captured and killed, and Balban appointed his son Bughra Khan as the iqtadar of Bengal.

subject: Medieval
question: Who was the first Mughal ruler who fought against the British?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The first conflict of the Mughals with the English (British) took place in 1686 A. D. during the reign of Aurangzeb. The Mughal governor Shaista Khan drove out the English, including Job Charnock, from Hugli (Hooghly).

subject: Modern History
question: Which of the following were the social reforms introduced by William Bentinck? 1. Abolition of Sati 2. Abolition of slavery 3. Removal of disabilities due to change of religion 4. Suppression of the organized bands of Thugs.
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Lord William Bentinck became the Governor General of Bengal presidency in 1828 A. D. In 1829 A. D., he declared the 'practice of sati' a crime and abolished it. Bentick tried to suppress thugs by running a campaign against the gang of thugs. Bentinck also worked on education and freedom of the press. In the time period of Bentinck, Charter Act, 1833 was passed which abolished slavery. In 1835 he went back to England. The provision of disqualifi cation due to change of religion was removed in 1850 A. D. Hence, statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct, so option (D) will be the answer.

subject: Geography
question: At which of the following places the newsprint paper industry is located?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Nepanagar is an industrial town located in Burhanpur district of Madhya Pradesh and is well known for the newsprint paper industry.

subject: Geography
question: Where was first coal mine in India mined?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The first coal mine in India was dug at Raniganj, on the bank of the Damodar River. This work began in 1774 A. D. as an exploration/discovery, whereas regular mining is considered to have started from 1820.

subject: Geography
question: According to the Census of India, 2011, which Scheduled Tribe is largest in India?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: As per Census 2011, the Bhil tribal group has the highest population among Scheduled Tribes in India. After that, the Gond tribal group has the second-highest population.

subject: Bihar Special
question: The total geographical area of Bihar State is
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: After the formation of Jharkhand State on 15 November 2000, Bihar’s present area is 94,163 sq km. This is about 2.86% of India’s total area. In terms of area, it stands at 13th position overall among the States and Union Territories of India (after including the Union Territory of Ladakh).

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which river is known as Sorrow of Bihar?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Kosi is known as the Sorrow of Bihar. Total length of Kosi is 729 km; it travels 260 km in Bihar. Canals on Kosi: East Kosi, West Kosi and Rajpur Canal.

subject: Bihar Special
question: In which district of Bihar, Telhar Kund Waterfall is located?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The Telhar (Telhar/Talhar) Kund waterfall is located in Kaimur district of Bihar.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which is the Asia's largest and freshwater oxbow lake in Bihar?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Kanwar Lake (Kabar Tal Wetland), Asia’s largest freshwater oxbow lake and bird sanctuary, located in Begusarai district of Bihar, was included in the list of Ramsar sites in July, 2020. It is Bihar’s first Ramsar site and the 39th Ramsar site of India.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which district of Bihar has the largest gold reserve?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The entire recorded gold ore resource of Bihar is associated with Jamui district. Indian Minerals Year Book 2024, As of 1 April 2020, the total gold ore (primary) reserves/resources in Bihar are recorded as 222,884,860 tonnes.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which district of Bihar is known as 'silk city'?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: In Bihar, Bhagalpur is known as the 'Silk City'. This city is situated on the southern bank of the Ganga River. Bhagalpur is world-famous for sericulture, the production of silk yarn, and silk-based products.

subject: Bihar Special
question: What is the female literacy rate of Bihar as per the Census 2011 of India?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: According to the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate in Bihar is 51.5 percent, and the male literacy rate is 71.2 percent.

subject: Geography
question: Which is the chief heavenly body of solar system?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The chief celestial body of the solar system is the Sun. The Sun is located at the center of the solar system.

subject: Geography
question: Which elements are abundant in the formation of interior layer of the earth?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: In the formation of the Earth’s inner layer “Nife”, the elements Nickel and Iron are found in abundance. Nife is an abbreviation of Nickel (Ni) and Iron (Fe).

subject: Geography
question: Who among the following postulated the concept of geographical cycle of erosion?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: W. M. Davis (William Morris Davis) presented the concept of the cycle of erosion. Walter Penck, while presenting a critical and alternative view of Davis’s theory, gave a model which he named “Morphological Analysis”.

subject: Geography
question: In which hemisphere, roaring forties, furious fifties and shrieking sixties are blowing?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, and Shrieking Sixties blow in the Southern Hemisphere. These names are given on the basis of the extreme intensity of the westerlies in the Southern Hemisphere.

subject: Geography
question: The Sargasso Sea is a part of the
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: The Sargasso sea is located in the North-Atlantic Ocean, it got its name from the Algae species 'Sargassum'. Four different currents surround this sea. Gulf Stream (warm) in the west, North Atlantic Current (Warm) in the North, Canary Current (cold) in the east and North Atlantic Equatorial (warm) current in the South. This sea has no coastline. The seaweed Sargassum here provides food to Turtles, shrimps, crabs, etc, hence ecologically it is rich but this seaweed sometimes creates problems in the navigation of ships.

subject: Geography
question: What is the boundary line between India and China called?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Sir Henry McMahon was the British negotiator. The line was negotiated after the Shimla conference in 1914. It was negotiated between Tibet and British India. China was not a part of this treaty and considers this line as illegal. During the 1950s, China occupied 'Aksai Chin' which led to the war in 1962, the boundary that came after the war is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC) between India and China. After the first Anglo-Burma war (1824-26), the British annexed Burma after signing the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826. Durand Line is between Afghanistan and Pakistan named after Mortimer Durand. Indira Point is the southernmost point of India, located on Nicobar Island, earlier it was known as Pygmalion Point or Parsons Point. Radcliffe Line is named after the chairman of the Border Commission 'Cyril Radcliffe' is the line between India and Pakistan.

subject: Geography
question: Rajasthan receives very little rain because
option_a: there is no water available and thus the winds remain dry
option_b: the winds do not come across any barriers to cause the necessary uplift to cool the air
option_c: the monsoon fails to reach this area
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
answer_text: the winds do not come across any barriers to cause the necessary uplift to cool the air
explanation: Rajasthan receives very little rainfall because the winds do not cross any major barrier, due to which they do not reach the height required for cooling. The Aravalli ranges, being aligned along the direction of the South-West Monsoon winds, do not act as an effective barrier in their path.

subject: Geography
question: Consider the following statements : 1. In India, the Project Tiger was launched in 1973. 2. The theme for National Biodiversity in 2022 is 'Building a shared future for all life'. 3. The Project Tiger is a tiger conservation programme. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: All three statements are correct: (1) Project Tiger was launched by the Government of India on 1 April 1973; (2) the UN International Day for Biological Diversity 2022 theme was 'Building a shared future for all life'; and (3) Project Tiger is India's flagship centrally sponsored tiger conservation programme.

subject: Geography
question: For which cultivation Karewas are famous?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Karewa consists of deposits of various types of soils and sediments such as sand, clay, silt, shale, lignite and loess. Karewa is famous for the cultivation of Zafran (local saffron)

subject: Geography
question: Which State in India is the leading producer of thorium?
option_e: None of the above/More than one of the above
explanation: Among the given options, Kerala is the leading state with respect to thorium. Monazite is the principal source of thorium. IREL (India) Limited separates thorium through chemical processing of monazite at its plant located at Udyogamandal (Aluva) in Ernakulam district.

subject: Polity
question: The phrase 'equality before law' used in Article 14 of the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution states that the State (India) shall not deny to any person within its territory equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. A special feature of this provision is that it applies equally to citizens as well as foreigners. Here, “equality before law” is taken from the British tradition (since Britain/Great Britain does not have a written constitution). The concept of “equal protection of the laws” has been taken from the American Constitution.

subject: Polity
question: What was the duration in the making of the Indian Constitution?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: From the beginning of drafting to the adoption of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly took a total of 2 years, 11 months and 18 days. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December, 1946, while the Constitution was adopted on 26 November, 1949.

subject: Polity
question: The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Article 164: The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to the state Legislative Assembly — mirroring Article 75(3) for the Union.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements : In the post-73rd Amendment era, there has to be decentralization of 1. decision-making powers 2. system as a whole 3. judicial powers 4. administrative powers. Which of the above statements are correct?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: 73rd Amendment provides decentralization of: Decision-making Power (Art.243G); Administrative powers (Governor appoints CEO of Zilla Parishad); Financial powers (State Finance Commission — Art.243I); System as a whole (third layer of executive created). Does NOT address judicial decentralization — India has three levels: SC, High Courts, Subordinate Courts.

subject: Polity
question: The representation in the Rajya Sabha includes
option_b: members indirectly elected by citizens through their representatives
option_c: members nominated by the President of India
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: More than one of the above
explanation: Article 80(1), sub-clauses (a) and (b) provide respectively that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of 12 members nominated by the President and not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories (Total—250). Under Article 80(4), the representatives of each State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of that State in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Thus, their election is indirect, through representatives chosen by the citizens. Under Article 80(5), the representatives of the Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha shall be chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law prescribe.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is concerned with the Supreme Court of India?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: More than one of the above
explanation: The Collegium system is the mechanism for the appointment of judges in the Supreme Court and High Courts, and for the transfer of High Court judges. It is a system developed through Supreme Court decisions. The Chief Justice of India leads the Collegium. Article 131 describes the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, while Articles 132 to 136 deal with its appellate jurisdiction. Hence, more than one option is correct.

subject: Polity
question: The minimum age for contesting elections to the Panchayati Raj Institutions should be how many years according to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. Under this, the minimum age for a person to become a Panchayat member is 21 years.

subject: Polity
question: With reference to the Consumer Disputes Redressal at the district level in India, which one of the following statements is not correct?
option_a: The State Government can establish more than one District Forum in a district if it deems fit.
option_b: One of the members of the District Forum shall be a woman.
option_c: The District Forum entertains the complaints where the value of goods or services does not exceed rupees fifty lakhs.
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: The District Forum entertains the complaints where the value of goods or services does not exceed rupees fifty lakhs.
explanation: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 provides a three-tier quasi-judicial mechanism for the resolution of consumer disputes, which includes the District Commission, State Commission, and National Commission. Under this Act, the State Government shall establish a District Commission and, if it deems fit, may establish more than one District Commission in a district. The District Commission consists of a President (qualified to be a District Judge) and at least two members; at least one among the President or the members must be a woman (and the minimum age for both the President and members is 35 years). The jurisdiction of the District Commissions includes complaints where the value paid for goods or services does not exceed `50 lakh.

subject: Polity
question: At what level does a Panchayat Samiti operate a Panchayati Raj structure?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: In the light of the provisions of the 73rd Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1992, the Bihar Panchayati Raj Act, 2006 has been enacted. Under it, Gram Panchayat is formed at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.

subject: Polity
question: Which one of the following was established as the first programme of community development?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: In India, for community development, the Cooperation Movement was first started in the second half of the 19th century. For this, the Cooperative Societies Act, 1904 was passed. The main objective of this programme was to support the Community Development Programme. In the question, the Hindi version used the term “Sahyog Andolan” (Cooperation Movement), which is an incorrect term. For this, in English the Commission used the term “Cooperation Movement.”

subject: Economics
question: Which of the following are the objectives of the SEZ Act, 2005? 1. Generation of additional economic activity 2. Promotion of exports of goods and services 3. Creation of employment
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Objectives of SEZ Act 2005 include: generation of additional economic activity, promotion of exports of goods and services, promotion of investment from domestic and foreign sources, creation of employment opportunities, and development of infrastructure facilities. All three stated objectives are correct.

subject: Economics
question: What is the policy measure adopted by the Government of India to improve the system of agricultural marketing?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: More than one of the above
explanation: Agricultural marketing involves assembling, storage, processing, transportation, packaging, grading and distribution of agricultural commodities. Government policy measures include: (i) MSP assurance, (ii) maintenance of buffer stocks of wheat and rice by FCI, and (iii) distribution of food grains and sugar through PDS. All A, B and C are correct — answer is D.

subject: Economics
question: Which committee suggested the enactment of the Competition Act, 2002?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 (MRTP Act) was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002 on recommendations of the S.V.S. Raghavan Committee. CCI was duly constituted in March 2009.

subject: Economics
question: Match List-I with List-II : a. Grey Revolution, b. Pink Revolution, c. Silver Revolution, d. Red Revolution / 1. Onion production, 2. Tomato and meat production, 3. Production of eggs, 4. Fertilizers
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Grey Revolution – Fertilizer Pink Revolution – Production of onion Silver Revolution – Production of eggs Red Revolution – Production of tomato and meat

subject: Economics
question: Which of the following Five-Year Plans was focussed on Human Resource Development?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: The SEVENTH Five-Year Plan (1985-90) was focused on Human Resource Development. 'Human resources development has necessarily to be assigned a key role in any development strategy.' PM: Rajiv Gandhi. Dr Manmohan Singh was Vice Chairman of Planning Commission from 1985-87. Target growth: 5%, Actual: 5.8%. Since none of the given options (Third, Fifth, First) is the Seventh Plan, the answer is E (None of the above).

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which of the following States of India received the highest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) equity flow during April to September 2022?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: India recorded highest-ever annual FDI inflow of USD 83.57 billion in FY 2021-22. Karnataka topped the FDI list for 2021-22 attracting Rs 1,62,830 crore, followed by Maharashtra at Rs 1,14,964 crore. Top FDI equity inflows: Singapore (27%), USA (18%). Computer Software and Hardware is the top recipient sector (~25% share).

subject: Economics
question: In which budget did the Finance Minister announce the Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: In March 1992, the Indian government implemented LERMS (Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System). Dr Manmohan Singh announced it in his 1992 budget (Union Budget 1992-93). LERMS introduced partial convertibility — 40% of foreign exchange earnings surrendered at official rate, 60% at market-determined rate. Based on C. Rangarajan Committee recommendations.

subject: Economics
question: Which of the following were goals of the Five-Year Plans? 1. Growth 2. Modernization 3. Self-reliance 4. Literature
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: The goals of the Five-Year Plans were: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity. Literature was NOT one of the objectives. All options A, B, C include 'Literature' which is wrong. The correct set (Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance, Equity) is not listed as an option. Hence E (None of the above is a completely correct set).

subject: Economics
question: Which organization carries out the survey for determining the poverty line?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Poverty estimation is carried out by NITI Aayog's task force through poverty line calculation based on data captured by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under MoSPI. NSSO was established in 1950. Key poverty committees: Alagh (1979), Lakdawala (1993), Tendulkar (2009), Rangarajan (2012). NSSO conducts the surveys; NITI Aayog uses the data.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The trade balance of India (merchandise and services) for December 2022 (provisional) is
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: India's overall export (Merchandise and Services combined) was USD 61.82 Billion in December 2022 (negative growth of -5.26% YoY). Overall import was USD 73.80 Billion (negative growth of -1.95% YoY). Trade balance = 61.82 - 73.80 = -11.98 USD billion.

subject: Bihar Special
question: At what percentage has Bihar registered the lowest Female Workforce Participation Rate for the year 2020-2022?
option_a: 4% in rural and 6.5% in urban areas
option_b: 6% in rural and 8.1% in urban areas
option_c: 7% in rural and 9.1% in urban areas
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: 4% in rural and 6.5% in urban areas
explanation: According to the data released by the National Sample Survey Office (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India), in 2020–21 and 2021–22, Bihar recorded the lowest female workforce participation rate (15 years and above) among all states of India. In 2020–21 and 2021–22, the female workforce participation rate in Bihar was, respectively, 11.2 percent and 10.1 percent in rural areas, and 6.3 percent and 10.5 percent in urban areas. According to the data for 2023–24, the female workforce participation rate in rural and urban areas is 33.1 percent and 15.5 percent, respectively. It is noteworthy that the Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (b) as the correct answer to this question.

subject: Bihar Special
question: The maximum number of tea industries in Bihar is in which district?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Kishanganj district in northeastern Bihar (part of the humid Terai–Dooars agro-climatic zone) accounts for the maximum tea cultivation and tea-processing industries in Bihar.

subject: Bihar Special
question: According to the National Family Survey-5 released by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on November 24, 2021, there has been a significant improvement in the sex ratio of Bihar. It has increased from ____ in 2015-2016 to ____ in 2020-2022.
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: As per NFHS-5, sex ratio in Bihar increased from 1062 in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 1090 in 2020-2022. Other NFHS-5 facts: Child sex ratio-908; Total fertility rate-3.0; Infant Mortality Rate-46.8.

subject: Bihar Special
question: According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021-2022), what was the rate of growth of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Bihar in 2020-2021?
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021–2022), due to the impact of COVID-19 and the lockdown, Bihar’s Gross State Domestic Product increased by only 2.5 percent in 2020–2021. According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2024–25), in 2023–24, Bihar’s per capita Gross State Domestic Product increased by 12.8 percent at current prices and by 7.6 percent at constant prices (2011–12) compared to the previous year.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which one of the following is correct for Bihar economy?
option_a: The growth rate is one of the lowest in India at 2.5%.
option_c: The occupational structure of the economy is stagnant from above.
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
answer_text: More than one of the above
explanation: The occupational structure of Bihar’s economy is stagnant in nature at the upper level. Bihar’s economy is mainly based on agriculture (the primary sector). According to the Bihar Economic Survey (2021–22), due to the impact of the lockdown, the growth rate of Bihar’s GSDP at current prices in 2020–21 was 2.5 percent (2.4 percent as per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25), which was the lowest among all the states in India. question: The Swadeshi and Boycott were adopted as the methods of struggle for the first time during the

option_d: More than one of the above

explanation: The Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon, announced the Partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905 (some sources also mention 20 July 1905). In protest against this announcement, a historic meeting was held at the Calcutta Town Hall, where the formal declaration was made of the Swadeshi Movement. When the Partition of Bengal was implemented in October 1905, that day was observed as a “Day of Mourning”. On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore, it was also observed as “Rakhi Day”. Nationalists observed this day to demonstrate the unbroken unity of Bengal. On the lines of Tagore’s Shantiniketan, the Bengal National College was established. Very soon, many national schools were set up across the country. In March 1906, the National Council of Education was formed. The Swadeshi Movement raised the slogan of self-reliance and self-power. The question of self-support and self-reliance was linked with national self-respect, honour, and self-confidence. The Congress, in its Calcutta Session (1906), also passed four resolutions related to the Swadeshi Movement, the Boycott Movement, National Education, and Self-government. Thus, it is clear that in opposition to the Partition of Bengal, nationalists launched movements such as Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, and Self-government.

subject: Modern History
question: Which of the following statements are not correct regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement in the towns? 1. Only the upper caste and the rich took part in the movement. 2. The council elections were boycotted even by the Justice Party of Madras. 3. Thousands of students left government-controlled schools, headmasters and teachers resigned and lawyers gave up their practice.
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: • During the years 1919-1922 A. D., two mass movements emerged in India as a means to oppose British rule: the Khilafat movement and the Non-Cooperation Movement. The non-cooperation Movement marked the beginning of the Gandhian Movement against British colonialism. • The movement saw significant participation from students, who left government-established schools and colleges in large numbers to join the cause. However, as the movement progressed, some of them began to harbour reservations about Gandhi's program. Hence statement 3 is correct. • Indian business groups, benefi ting from the emphasis on Swadeshi (indigenous production and boycott of foreign goods) by the nationalists, supported the economic boycott called for during the movement. • Peasants also actively participated in the movement, but it did lead to confrontations between different castes, particularly between the lower and upper castes. • Initially, the movement was led by individuals from the middle classes, but as time passed, many of them expressed reservations about Gandhi's approach. Hence statement 1 is incorrect. • The Non-Cooperation Movement provided an opportunity for the oppressed masses to express their grievances against both the British and their Indian oppressors. • Women played a crucial role in the movement, participating in large numbers, giving up purdah (seclusion) and contributing their ornaments to the Tilak Fund. • The movement faced violent reprisals from the police, resulting in the loss of many lives. • Regarding the Justice Party, which was active in the Madras Presidency, it did not support the Non-Cooperation Movement. The party sought to work within the existing political system and preferred continued British presence. They disagreed with Mahatma Gandhi, particularly due to his praise for Brahminism. Hence statement 2 is incorrect. • In summary, the Non-Cooperation Movement saw widespread participation from various sections of society, but as it progressed, some segments showed reservations, and it also faced opposition from political groups like the Justice Party.

question: In lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, _____ live together.
option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: In lichens, a chlorophyll-containing partner—algae (phycobiont)—and a chlorophyll-lacking partner—fungus (mycobiont)—live together. This is called mutualism. In this type of association, the fungus is the more dominant partner. The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae, and in return, the algae provides food to the fungus, which it prepares through photosynthesis. In lichens, reproduction occurs through the fungal component. In biology, when two organisms help each other, it is called a symbiotic (Mutualism) relationship.

explanation: Female Anopheles can be distinguished from female Culex because it rests at an angle to the substratum. Globally, more than 3,500 species of mosquitoes are found, and they are divided into three genera—Culex, Anopheles, and Aedes. Each genus works as an intermediate host for a specific parasite. Besides this, there are sufficient differences among them in terms of food chain, shape, habitat, etc. Difference between Culex and Anopheles– Culex Their eggs are laid in clusters on the surface of water. Their larvae feed from below. Their wings are transparent. They are capable of flying long distances. Their body remains parallel to the substratum. Anopheles Eggs are laid separately (not in clusters) on the water surface. They lay eggs in a horizontal pattern. Their larvae feed from above. Their wings are spotted. They cannot fly long distances. Their body rests at an angle to the substratum.

option_d: More than one of the above
option_e: None of the above
explanation: Lymphocyte is the most important cell type related to the body’s immunity because it is the WBC that secretes the maximum amount of antibody proteins. Lymphocytes are formed in the bone marrow and are found in blood and lymphatic tissues. Lymphocytes are mainly of two types— B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. Notably, in response to pathogens, B-lymphocytes produce a chain of proteins in human blood so that they can fight pathogens. These proteins are called antibodies (Antibodies). T-lymphocytes do not secrete antibodies themselves, but they help Blymphocytes in producing these proteins (antibodies). These are important parts of the immune system, which protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens.
