Wave Motion - Mechanical waves can only be created in elastic and inertia-containing media. - In transverse wave, oscillation occurs perpendicular to the direction of energy-transfer. - It usually occurs in elastic solids and only emerges on liquid surfaces. - Gases do not give rise to transverse waves. - In longitudinal waves, oscillation takes place in the wave's direction. - It comes from all types of media, such as solids, liquids, and gases. viz...Sound - Time period decreases with the increase in the frequency of waves. (T α 1/f) - Electromagnetic waves do not need any medium for propagation. - In e-m wave, electric field and magnetic field are mutually perpendicular, and also both these fields are perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave. - They travel with a speed equal to the speed of light in a vacuum. - Velocity of electromagnetic waves is 3 × 10⁸ ms⁻¹. - Speed of all electromagnetic waves is the same. - Electromagnetic waves' energy varies with their wavelength, with shorter wavelengths having a higher energy and longer wavelengths having a lower energy. - Examples- Gamma rays, X-rays, UV rays, visible radiation, infrared rays, shortwave radio waves, and longwave radio waves. - Stationary and Transverse types of sound vibrations are produced in Sitar. - Cosmic rays are highly energetic charged particles originating from the sun. They have very short wavelengths. - Ionosphere reflects back the long radio waves. - Space waves normally propagate the waves of the ultra-high frequency range. - The distance between two successive crests or successive troughs is known as wavelength. - In contrast to gamma rays, which have the smallest wavelength, radio waves have the largest. - Wavelength order: Radio waves > microwave > Infrared > visible light > Ultraviolet > X-ray > Gamma rays. - The structure of crystals is ascertained using X-rays. - An enemy aircraft's existence can be found via radio waves. - A night vision device makes use of infrared wavelengths. - Infrared waves are used in TV remote control. - Microwaves are used in telecommunications. - FM broadcasting uses an 88-108 MHz frequency range. - X-rays are used for the diagnosis of intestinal diseases and CT scans. Sound - Sound travels in solids as both longitudinal waves and transverse waves, while in plasma, gases, and liquids it travels as longitudinal waves. - Speed of sound depends upon the nature of the medium and temperature. - It is fastest in solids while slowest in gases. - It cannot travel through a vacuum. - The speed of sound increases with an increase in temperature. - However, in comparison to dry air, wet air has a higher sound speed, because the density of moist air is less than that of dry air. As the velocity of sound in gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its density, the velocity of sound in moist air is greater than that in dry air. - Our ears are only capable of hearing sound waves with a frequency range of 20 Hz to 20000 Hz i.e. Audible sound waves. - Infrasonic waves have frequencies that are below 20 Hz i.e., below the frequency of audible sound. - Lots of animals such as pigeons, elephants, rhinoceroses, hippopotamuses, giraffes, and cuttlefish can sense Infrasonic sound. - Volcanoes, earthquakes, and meteors are among the natural sources of infrasound. - Many creatures, including dolphins, whales, and bats, have the ability to create ultrasonic waves, which has a frequency of more than 20000 Hz. - An echo is a sound that results from sound waves returning to the listener after being reflected off a surface. - To clearly hear the echo, there must be a distance of atleast 16.5 meters between the listener and the reflector. - The Mach number is the ratio of a body's speed to the speed of sound in the environment. - Bel is the unit of sound intensity, while decibel, which is one-tenth of a bel, is more frequently used. - The optimum sound level for humans is 60 decibels and a sound higher than 80 decibels can damage the ear. Speed of sound in various mediums: | Medium | Speed/(m/s) | Medium | Speed/(m/s) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Rubber | 60 m/s | Glass | 4540 m/s | | Air at 0℃ | 331 m/s | Copper | 4600 m/s | | Air at 20℃ | 343 m/s | Aluminium | 6420 m/s | | Air at 40℃ | 355 m/s | Iron | 5950 m/s | | Hydrogen (25℃) | 1284 m/s | Steel | 5960 m/s | - Halls designed for music concerts should have sound-absorbing walls to prevent echo. - Pitch of sound depends upon frequency. - Due to the lack of atmosphere on the moon, astronauts cannot hear each other. - Multiple sound reflections from the stethoscope allow the doctor to hear the patient's heartbeat. - Sound's speed, wavelength, and amplitude change when it travels from one medium to another, while its frequency remains constant. - A sound's amplitude, which is a measure of its loudness, diminishes with increasing distance from the source. - Basic unit of sound is phonemes. - Frequency modulation is used to transmit audio signals on television. Electric Current and Conductivity: - Electric current refers to the rate at which an electric charge moves across a conductor. - Positive charge flow is regarded as the direction of electric current flow. - Electric currents are of two types: direct current and alternating current. - The main benefit of alternating current over direct current is that it can be transmitted across great distances with little electric loss. - The SI unit of electric power is watt but for commercial purposes kilowatt-hour is used which is popularly known as unit. - 1 unit = 1 kilowatt hour = 1000 watt hour. - Value of 1 unit is 3.6 × 10⁶ Joule. - No heat is lost when electrical energy is transformed into motion. - The electromagnetic induction theory underlies the operation of electric motors and dynamos. - When working at low voltages, electric motors are more likely to burn out as a result of drawing more current, which is inversely proportional to voltage. - Reason: As the Power (P) of motor is constant, and P=VI ie. I=P/V, which means Current is inversely proportional to Voltage, such that when voltage is low, current is high, and this high current causes power loss (I²R) by producing large heat and thus burning the motor. - Faraday constant is a universal constant. - Nickel-cadmium batteries are used in calculators, transistors, flashlights, portable power tools, etc. - Tungsten is used as a filament in lighting bulbs. - The Halogen lamp filament is an alloy of tungsten and sodium, and due to sodium, it emits yellow light. - Fuse wire used for the safety of the house has high resistance and low melting point. - CFL (compact Fluorescent lamp) has a lifespan of about 6000 and 10000 hours and emits light using mercury vapour and phosphor. - LED lamps are more energy-efficient and have a lifespan of roughly 50000 hours. They produce light using semiconductor material. - LED works on the principle of electroluminescence. - Fluorescent tubes are filled with noble gases such as argon, neon, and xenon, as well as low-pressure gases like mercury. - Nitrogen and argon gases are filled in the electric bulbs, to prevent the oxidation of Tungsten filament used in the bulb. - Parallel connections are used in home electrical wiring. - White light is produced by oscillating the molecules in the tube. - A colour code for wires is used in wiring to avoid confusion viz. black for neutral, red for live wire, and green for earth wire. - Transformers are used for step-up or step-down AC voltages. - Mobile phone charger is a step-down transformer. - AC current is not preferable to charge storage batteries. - AC current is converted into DC current using a rectifier. - Germanium and silicon are used as semiconductors in transistors. - Silicons are used in solar cells or photovoltaic cells. - Silver, copper, aluminum, and iron are the best conductor of electricity as they are the most electrically conductive element. - Zero permeability is the characteristic feature of superconductors. - Ceramic oxides viz... Mercury, calcium, barium, and thallium, are newly discovered high-temperature superconductors. - Resistance of semiconductors decreases with the increase in temperature and at absolute zero temperature the electric resistance in semiconductors is infinite. Nuclear Physics - Photons, deuterons, and alpha particles are accelerated by cyclotrons. - The ultimate source of energy in stars and the sun is hydrogen which changes into helium due to nuclear fusion. - Uranium 235 or plutonium 239 are used as fuel in nuclear reactors, previously known as atomic piles or molecular furnaces," and when these fissile atomic nuclei absorb a neutron, they may undergo nuclear fission. - With the release of kinetic energy, the heavy nucleus is divided into two or more lighter nuclei, free neutrons as well as gamma rays. - H₂O (light water), D₂O (heavy water), graphite, or beryllium oxide are used as moderators to slow down the neutrons in this reaction, which is also known as a self-sustaining chain reaction. - As a nuclear fuel, radioactive elements such as thorium, plutonium, and uranium are used. - The principle of an atomic bomb is based on the uncontrolled nuclear fission of uranium while a hydrogen bomb is based upon the uncontrolled nuclear fusion of deuterium and tritium (isotopes of hydrogen). - The nuclear doctrine of India contains no first use, unilateral moratorium, and minimum credible deterrence.

subject: Physics
question: The image formed by concave mirror is real, inverted and of the same size as that of the object. The position of the object should be
option_c: between the focus and centre of curvature
explanation: If an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, then the image formed is real, inverted and of the same size as that of the object. The image formed is not magnified. M A D B P B′ C F E A′ N

subject: Physics
question: A photoelectric cell is a device which
option_a: converts light energy into electric energy
option_b: converts electric energy into light energy
answer_text: converts light energy into electric energy
explanation: A photoelectric cell is an electronic device that converts light energy into electrical energy. It is also called an Electric Eye or a Phototube. Note that a photoelectric cell works on the principle of the photoelectric effect. A photoelectric cell consists of an evacuated glass tube in which two electrodes are fitted—an emitter and a collector.

subject: Chemistry
question: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as _____ in Chemistry.
explanation: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass is called the concentration of the solution in chemistry. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components. A homogeneous mixture means that the composition and properties are uniform throughout. Generally, the component present in larger quantity is called the solvent. The solvent determines the physical state in which the solution exists. Besides the solvent, one or more components present in the solution are called solutes.

subject: Biology
question: How do COVID vaccines stimulate an immune response?
option_a: By introducing live attenuated SARS-CoV-2 virus
option_b: By introducing a real SARS-CoV-2 virus
option_c: By introducing a harmless piece of SARS-CoV-2 virus
option_d: By introducing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 virus
answer_text: By introducing a harmless piece of SARS-CoV-2 virus
explanation: COVID vaccines stimulate the immune response by introducing a harmless part of the SARS-CoV-2 virus (such as the spike protein) or instructions to make it, so the body produces antibodies and develops immune memory.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following liquids is a bad conductor of electricity?
explanation: Lemon juice, salted water, and orange juice contain dissolved ions, due to which these solutions show conductivity. All of these are conductors of electricity. Therefore, among the given options, (d) is the correct answer.

subject: Biology
question: The DNA double helix structure was discovered by
explanation: It is a misconception that Dr. James Watson, Dr. Francis Crick, M. H.F. Wilkins, and Rosalind Franklin discovered DNA. In fact, on the basis of Wilkins’ X-ray analysis, Watson and Crick presented the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953. Actually, DNA was first identified in 1869 by the Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher. Friedrich called it “nuclein.”

subject: Physics
question: Two objects of different masses falling freely near the surface of the Moon would
option_b: undergo a change in their inertia
option_c: have same velocity at any instant
answer_text: have same velocity at any instant
explanation: In free fall, the acceleration g is independent of mass. The relation for velocity is v = u + gt, so velocity depends not only on initial velocity (u) and time (t). Hence, if two objects are released together from the same point (neglecting air resistance) under identical initial conditions (e. g., u = 0), then at any instant their velocities will be the same.

subject: Biology
question: How do vector vaccines work to provide immunity?
option_a: By introducing a weakened or inactivated virus into the body
option_b: By directly attacking and destroying pathogens in the body
option_c: By placing the virus in a modified version of a different virus
option_d: By entering directly into the cells and enabling them to create spike proteins
answer_text: By placing the virus in a modified version of a different virus
explanation: Vector vaccines work to provide immunity by using a modified version of another virus to deliver the required genetic material into the body. This enables the body to produce the target antigen and develop an immune response.

subject: Geography
question: The process that continually adds new crust is
explanation: The process that continuously adds new layers is seafloor spreading. This hypothesis was proposed by Harry H. Hess (in the 1960s). It was published in 1962 in a research paper titled “History of Ocean Basins”

subject: Geography
question: The theory that states “pieces of the Earth’s crust are in constant, slow motion driven by movement in the mantle” is called
explanation: The theory states that pieces (plates) of the Earth’s crust keep moving slowly due to mantle motion is the Plate Tectonics Theory. According to this theory, the Earth’s crust is divided into many small and large plates. These tectonic plates move independently in different directions over the asthenosphere. The various landforms produced due to these plate movements are studied under plate tectonics.

subject: Biology
question: What is the expanded form of the term ‘mRNA’ that has been widely discussed since the beginning of the pandemic?
explanation: The expanded form of mRNA is Messenger Ribonucleic acid. Messenger RNA is a type of single-stranded RNA that is involved in protein synthesis. mRNA-based vaccines were developed to prevent COVID-19.

subject: Physics
question: An AC current can be produced by
explanation: AC (Alternating Current) can be generated by a dynamo. A dynamo works on the principle of electromagnetic induction and converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

subject: Physics
question: Current density is
explanation: The current flowing through unit cross-sectional area is called current density. It is a vector quantity, and its direction is the same as the direction of current. Its SI unit is A/m².

subject: Chemistry
question: What is the basis of most useful classification of medications in medical chemistry?
explanation: In medicinal chemistry, drugs are classified on the basis of chemical structure, pharmacological effect, solubility, and molecular target. Among these, classification based on the molecular target is considered the most useful.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following slows down the reaction rate?
explanation: In the given options, all are related to catalysts, which affect the rate of a chemical reaction. A catalyst works to increase the rate of a chemical reaction. The rate of any chemical reaction depends on the concentration of reactants, catalyst, temperature, and the nature of reactants. Therefore, the correct option is (d).

subject: Biology
question: Input and output nerves meet at
explanation: Afferent (Sensory) and efferent (Motor) nerve impulses originated from the central nervous system. The central nervous system (CNS) is the processing center of the nervous system. The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord. The major functions of the CNS are processing information, controlling blood pressure and respiration, and regulating and coordinating body functions, etc. The CNS works like the central processing unit (CPU) of the body.

subject: Current Affairs
question: In the context of ‘Shipwreck Tourism’, shipwrecks in Indian waters have been explored at Sunchi Reef, Amee Shoals and Grande Island. Where are these locations?
option_c: Off the coast of Tamil Nadu
explanation: In the context of ‘Shipwreck Tourism’, shipwrecks have been located in Indian waters at Sunchi Reef, Amee Shoals, and Grande Island. These places are off the Goa coast. It is noteworthy that there are many references regarding shipwrecks; however, the exact locations of all of them are not known.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The G20 members represent 1. around 85% of the global GDP 2. about 50% of the global trade 3. about two-thirds of the world population Which of the above statistics is/are correct?
explanation: The G20 includes 19 countries (Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Türkiye, the United Kingdom, and the United States) along with the European Union and the African Union. G20 members represent about 85% of global GDP, while in terms of global trade this figure is above 75%. They represent about two-thirds of the world’s total population. Thus, option (B) is the correct answer.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Who is the Head of Russia’s Wagner Mercenary Group?
explanation: Yevgeny Prigozhin was the founder and leader of Russia's Wagner Private Military (Mercenary) Group; he died in an aircraft crash in Tver Oblast in August 2023 shortly after leading a brief mutiny in June 2023.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The Global Gender Gap Report is released by
explanation: The Global Gender Gap Report is released by the World Economic Forum. According to the Global Gender Gap Report, 2025, India’s rank is 131st. Among India’s neighbouring countries, Pakistan, China and Bangladesh were ranked 148th, 103rd and 24th respectively. It is noteworthy that in the 2023 edition of this report, India was ranked 127th.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which one of the following statements regarding Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom is correct?
option_a: She reigned for 70 years and died at the age of 96 years.
option_b: She reigned for 68 years and died at the age of 94 years.
option_c: She reigned for 72 years and died at the age of 92 years.
option_d: She reigned for 66 years and died at the age of 90 years.
answer_text: She reigned for 70 years and died at the age of 96 years.
explanation: Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms. She reigned for 70 years (1952-2022 AD) and died at the age of 96 years (1926-2022 AD).

subject: Current Affairs
question: What was the theme of DefExpo–2022, held in Gujarat?
option_a: India : The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub
explanation: DefExpo-2022 was held in October 2022 in Gandhinagar, the capital of Gujarat. The theme of this event was ‘Path to Pride’. In this five-day programme, businesspersons, investors, start-ups, the armed forces, and representatives of many countries participated.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The three-day celebration of Thadingyut Festival is celebrated in which country?
explanation: Thadingyut festival is organised in Myanmar. It is celebrated as festival of light in Myanmar to commemorate the full moon of the summer lunar month Thadingyut.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Consider the following statements regarding the ‘White House’ : 1. The address of the White House is 1800 Pennsylvania Avenue. 2. It is the official residence and workplace of the President of USA. 3. On November 1, 1800, John Adams became the first President to take residence in the building. 4. It is a symbol of American Democracy. Which of the above statements are correct?
explanation: The “White House” is the residence of the U. S. President. Its foundation stone was laid in 1792. Thereafter, on 1 November, 1800, the then President John Adams and his wife Abigail moved in. Its official address is 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue. It is noteworthy that the “White House” is a symbol of American democracy.

subject: Current Affairs
question: ‘Net Metering’ is sometimes seen in the news in the context of promoting
option_a: the installation of CNG kits in motorcars
option_b: the installation of water meters in urban households
option_c: a billing mechanism for solar energy by consumers for the electricity they add to the grid
option_d: the use of piped natural gas in the kitchens of households

explanation: ‘Net Metering’ is a billing mechanism that credits solar power system owners for electricity fed into the grid. It is noteworthy that ‘Net Metering’ provides customers who use it an opportunity to efficiently adjust their electricity consumption.

question: What is the name of the deep-sea submersible that imploded during an underwater voyage to the Titanic wreckage?
explanation: On 18 June 2023, Titan, a deep-sea submersible operated by the American tourism and expeditions company OceanGate, imploded during an expedition to view the wreck of the Titanic in the North Atlantic Ocean off the coast of New Foundland, Canada.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Where did the former President of the USA give his interview recently?
explanation: As per the question and the given options, former U. S. President Barack Obama gave an interview in Athens in June, 2023.

subject: Current Affairs
question: In the context of sports, which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1. Flushing Meadows : French Open 2. Venus Rosewater Dish : Wimbledon Trophy (Women) 3. Roland Garros : US Open 4. Australian Open (Women) : Daphne Akhurst Memorial Cup
explanation: The women’s singles trophy related to Wimbledon is called the “Venus Rosewater Dish.” This trophy started in 1886. Its weight is about 2.3 kg. subject: Current Affairs
question: The Ministry of Home Affairs has completed the Mother Tongue Survey of India (MTSI) in November 2022 with field videography of the country’s how many languages?
explanation: India’s Union Ministry of Home Affairs completed the Mother Tongue Survey of India (MTSI) with field videography of 576 languages of the country. It may be noted that, in a report, the Ministry of Home Affairs emphasized preserving every indigenous mother tongue. According to this report, NIC and the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) will document and preserve the linguistic data of the surveyed mother tongues in audio-video files.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which State Government launched the State-Level Committee for Vulture Conservation (SLCVC), proposed by the national action for the protection of vultures in India?
explanation: In October, 2022 Government of Tamil Nadu launched the State-Level Committee for Vulture Conservation (SLCVC) for coordination between various wings of the government to implement the Action Plan for Vulture Conservation (APVC) 2020-2025.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Ten captive-bred Asian Giant Tortoises (Manouria emys), one of the largest tortoise species in mainland Asia, were recently released into which National Park of India?
explanation: Ten captive-bred Asian Giant Tortoises (Manouria emys), one of the largest tortoise species in mainland Asia, were released in December, 2022 into a protected area of Ntangki National Park of Nagaland.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which country has recently reaffirmed Arunachal Pradesh as an integral part of India?
explanation: In July, 2023, the U. S. Senate unanimously passed a resolution recognizing Arunachal Pradesh as an integral part of India. The resolution was introduced by Senators Jeff Merkley, Bill Hagerty, Tim Kaine, John Cornyn and Chris Van Hollen. It is noteworthy that the resolution stated that the United States recognizes the McMahon Line as the international boundary between China and Arunachal Pradesh (India).

subject: Current Affairs
question: India’s Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil won which medal in Men’s 10 m Air Rifle at the ISSF World Championship in Cairo?
explanation: Indian shooter Rudraksh Balasaheb Patil won the gold medal in the 10 metre air rifle individual event at the ISSF Shooting World Cup held in Cairo, Egypt in February 2023. The 19-year-old Rudraksh defeated Germany’s Maximilian Ulbrich in the final by a score of 16–8. It may be noted that Croatia’s Miran Maričić won the bronze medal. In the same tournament, this was Patil’s second gold; he also won the gold medal in the 10 metre air rifle mixed team event with Narmada Nitin Raju. Before this, Rudraksh qualified for the ranking matches by finishing 7th in the qualification round with a score of 629.3. After finishing first in the ranking matches, Rudraksh qualified for the gold medal match.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The National Education Policy, 2020 emphasizes the integration of vocational education into mainstream education from which grade onwards?
explanation: The National Education Policy, 2020 recommends starting vocational education from Grade 6 to provide all students with access to high-quality vocational education. This enables them to gain the skills needed for further education and training and to obtain a clear and recognized pathway to employment. As per the policy, all students will participate in a 10-day bagless period during Grades 6–8, where they will intern with local vocational experts such as carpenters, gardeners, potters, artists, etc. Similar internship opportunities for learning vocational subjects can be made available to students during Grades 6–12 (including vacation periods).

subject: Current Affairs
question: India signed the Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) with which country?
explanation: On 2 April 2022, India and Australia signed the India– Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (Ind-Aus ECTA). It is noteworthy that this agreement includes cooperation between the two friendly countries in the field of bilateral economic and commercial relations, and it also covers the following areas—  Trade in goods; rules of origin.  Trade in services.  Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT).  Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) measures.  Dispute settlement; temporary movement of persons.  Telecommunications; customs procedures and trade facilitation.  Cooperation in pharmaceutical products and other sectors.

subject: Current Affairs
question: The Plain Language Act was passed by which of the following countries recently which requires Government officials to use simple and easily understandable English language in official documents and websites?
explanation: In October 2022, New Zealand passed the Plain Language Act, under which public service agencies and Crown agents must use simple, easy-to-understand English for certain documents and website content prepared/published for the general public. The objective of this bill was to improve the effectiveness and accountability of the public service by ensuring that communication for the public is clear and accessible. According to the bill, plain language is language that is appropriate for the intended audience and is clear, concise, and well organised.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Tillyardembi Fossils of the world’s first plant pollinators, called Tillyardembiids, were discovered recently in which country?
explanation: In February 2023, scientists discovered 280-million-yearold, considered among the oldest known possible plant pollinators, called Tillyardembids. These were found on a riverbank near the village of Chekarda in Russia. According to researchers, these insect fossils were preserved in layers of sedimentary rocks formed during the Permian period. The Tillyardembiids were named after the British-Australian entomologist Robert John Tillyard, who worked on the study of ancient insect fossils

subject: Current Affairs
question: The ‘Lisbon Declaration’, which made headlines, is associated with the conservation of which entity?
explanation: The Lisbon Declaration is related to the conservation of oceans. It may be noted that in 2022, a five-day United Nations Ocean Conference was concluded, in which more than 150 countries collectively agreed to scale up science-based and innovative actions to address the marine emergency. The declaration, along with bold commitments from all sections of society—youth, civil society, businesses, and the scientific community—clearly demonstrates the centrality of a safe, healthy, and productive ocean for food security, livelihoods, and a secure planet. The conference was co-hosted by Portugal and Kenya. More than 100 countries joined the High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People, pledging to protect 30% of the world’s oceans by 2030.

subject: Ancient History
question: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
explanation: Among the given options, the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the bull and the elephant, but scholars differ regarding the presence of the horse. It is difficult to determine with certainty whether the bones obtained from various Harappan sites belong to the wild ass/ onager (Equus hemionus khur) or to the domesticated horse (Equus caballus). Evidence of the horse, or other animals of the same group, has been reported from Rangpur, Rana Ghundai, Lothal, Surkotada, Kuntasi and Kalibangan. A scholar reported that among the so-called horse remains found from Surkotada, six were genuine horse remains dating to around 2000 BCE, i. e., around the middle of the last part of the third millennium BCE. In 1974, J. P. Joshi and A. K. Sharma of the Archaeological Survey of India reported that horse bones were found at every level here between 2100– 1700 BCE. However, Ramsharan Sharma, Romila Thapar, Mando, etc., do not accept this. Similarly, the teeth claimed to be of a horse by Brigadier E. J. Ross from the Early Harappan site of Rana Ghundai are considered inauthentic by Zauner. Therefore, regarding the horse, it would be appropriate to say that its presence in the Harappan Civilization cannot be completely denied, though its use must have been extremely limited. The Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (b) as the answer.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
explanation: Khajuraho temples, Bhimbetka rock shelters and Sanchi stupa are listed among the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India. Mandu fort is not listed as the World Heritage Site.
