option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: Reserve Bank of India and NABARD
explanation: To provide farmers with affordable short-term crop loans, the Government of India runs the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS) and an additional scheme for the Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI). For transparent and faster settlement of claims, the Kisan Rin Portal (KRP) was launched in 2023. Before the launch of KRP, manual claims of interest subvention (IS) and prompt repayment incentive (PRI) were sent to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and NABARD. It is noteworthy that technically, farmers themselves did not directly send these claims to RBI or NABARD; rather, based on the loans given to farmers, banks sent these claims to RBI and NABARD. Therefore, the statement in the question that “farmers… submitted manual claims” is not technically correct.

subject: Economics
question: India's foreign exchange reserves:
option_a: Increased to around USD 640 billion as of the end of December 2024
option_b: Are seventh largest in the world
option_c: Decreased caused by a BoP deficit of around USD 24 billion in 2024
option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: Increased to around USD 640 billion as of the end of December 2024
explanation: According to the Government press release based on the synopsis of the Economic Survey 2024–25, by the end of December 2024 India’s foreign exchange reserves were 640.3 billion US dollars (about 640 billion). However, after crossing the 700-billion-dollar mark, they moderated to this level; they did not “increase” to this level. By the end of December 2024, India was the world’s fourth-largest holder of foreign exchange reserves (after China, Japan and Switzerland). As per the Balance of Payments (BoP) data released for the financial year 2024, the year’s total BoP was recorded as a surplus of about 63.7 billion US dollars (supplemented by a valuation gain of 4.3 billion US dollars), not as a deficit of 24 billion US dollars. In fact, in the first half of the financial year 2025 (April–September), with a BoP surplus of 23.9 billion US dollars, foreign exchange reserves increased by 59.4 billion US dollars. The Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (a) as the correct answer to this question. As of 16 January, 2026 India’s foreign exchange reserves stood at 701.4 billion US dollars.

subject: Economics
question: As per NFHS-5 data, which of the following state(s) recorded less than 6% of the population as multidimensionally poor in 2019-20?
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: According to the NFHS-5 based headcount ratio, the multidimensional poverty rate of the given States/Union Territories is as follows— Jammu and Kashmir (4.80%), Himachal Pradesh (4.93%), and Uttar Pradesh (22.93%). Thus, both Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have a multidimensional poverty rate below 6%. Since Jammu and Kashmir is a Union Territory, therefore, from the point of view of “states,” Himachal Pradesh will be the correct answer. Among all the States/Union Territories of India, the highest multidimensional poverty rate is recorded in Bihar (33.76%). It may be noted that NFHS-5 data pertains to 2019–21, whereas the question mentions 2019–20.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Match List-I with List-II: | List-I: (a) Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme, (b) Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), (c) Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, (d) National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) | List-II: 1. Introduced in the Union Budget for 2023-24, 2. Aims to reduce emissions in energy-intensive industries, 3. Launched in 2019 as a national-level strategy, 4. Launched at COP 26 in Glasgow in 2021
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: (a) PAT (Perform, Achieve, Trade): Related to Energy Efficiency (reducing emissions in energy-intensive industries). (Matches 2). (b) MISHTI: Mangrove Initiative (Shoreline Habitats), introduced in Union Budget 2023-24. (Matches 1) (c) Li FE (Lifestyle for Environment): Concept introduced by PM Modi at COP 26 in Glasgow (2021). (Matches 4). (d) NCAP (National Clean Air Programme): Launched in 2019 as a national strategy to tackle air pollution. (Matches 3).

subject: Economics
question: According to Annual PLFS 2023-24 report:
option_a: There is greater increase in Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) of rural females as compared to urban females since 2021-22.
option_b: Among the 36 states and union territories, 90% states have a Workforce Participation Rate (WPR) (for all ages) below the national average of 43.7 percent.
option_c: The share of female workers in agriculture has decreased significantly from 2017-18 to 2023-24.
option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: There is greater increase in Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) of rural females as compared to urban females since 2021-22.
explanation: According to the Annual Report of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2023-24, in 2021-22 the labour force participation rate of rural women (all ages) was 27.2%, which increased to 35.5% in 2023-24. During the same period, the labour force participation rate of urban women (all ages) was 18.8% and 22.3% respectively. Hence, since 2021-22, the labour force participation rate of rural women has increased more than that of urban women. Out of 36 states/Union Territories, in 24 states/Union Territories the worker population ratio (WPR) for all ages is above the national average (43.7%), while in 12 states/Union Territories it is below the national average. Thus, in 33.33% of states/Union Territories the WPR is below the national average. The share of female workers in the agricultural sector has increased in 2023-24 compared to earlier years. It increased from 57.0% in 2017-18 to 62.9% in 2021-22 and further to 64.4% in 2023-24. Therefore, option (a) is true, while options (b) and (c) are false.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which of the following was NOT the outcome of Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2020?
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: Among the given options, “One Nation, One Subscription” and the Research and Innovation Excellence Framework (RIEF) were proposed initiatives in the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2020, whereas the Atal Innovation Mission began in 2016.

subject: Economics
question: Share of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in the country's Gross Value Added (GVA) has increased from ____ in 2020-21 to ____ in 2022-23.
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: The share of MSME Gross Value Added (GVA) in India's total GVA dipped during the pandemic but recovered: 2020-21: 27.3% 2022-23:Recovered to roughly 30.1%.

subject: Economics
question: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct regarding the Indian cement industry? | 1. Around 87% of India's cement industry is concentrated in a few major states like Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. | 2. India is the largest producer of cement in the world. | 3. Most cement plants in India are located far from raw material sources and near the ports to support exports. | Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: Most cement plants are located near sources of raw materials (especially limestone). About 87% of the cement industry is concentrated in a few selected states such as Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Meghalaya and West Bengal. India still remains the world’s second-largest cement producer after China. Therefore, among the given statements, only statement 1 is correct.

subject: Bihar Special
question: What is the primary objective of Bihar's Mission Daksh?
option_a: To increase school enrolment in primary schools in rural areas.
option_b: To provide vocational training to teachers at senior-secondary level.
option_c: To offer personalised mentoring for lagging students to reach grade-level competencies.
option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: To offer personalised mentoring for lagging students to reach grade-level competencies.
explanation: The main objective of Mission Daksh is to identify students who are lagging behind in studies and provide them with personalised mentoring so that they can reach their gradelevel competencies.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which of the following is NOT one of the components under the YUVA framework of the Bihar Startup Policy 2022?
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: To support startups for youth and create an enabling ecosystem, the framework of the Bihar Startup Policy, 2022 has been prepared on the following four pillars— 1. Awareness, networking and mentoring campaigns. 2. Making startups free from regulators for support. 3. Encouraging and supporting startups through vibrancy in the education system. 4. Facilitating financial and incubation support. Therefore, there is no component included under this framework by the name “international market expansion plans”.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct about Bihar's economic performance in 2023-24?
option_a: Bihar's per capita GSDP at current prices increased by 12.8% in 2023-24 over the previous year.
option_b: The estimated share of the tertiary sector in Bihar's GSVA (constant prices) in 2023-24 was 58.6%.
option_c: The Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) formed 4.6% of GSDP at current prices in 2023-24.
option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: More than one of the above
explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in 2023–24 Bihar’s per capita GSDP at current prices increased by 12.8 percent over the previous year to approximately `66,828. At constant prices (2011–12), the estimated share of the tertiary (service) sector in Bihar’s Gross State Value Added for 2023–24 was 58.6 percent. Gross Fixed Capital Formation at current prices increased from 1.6 percent of GSDP in 2019–20 to 4.6 percent of GSDP in 2023–24.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Consider the following statements: | 1. The proportion of the young population (0-19 years) in Bihar is projected to decline significantly by 2041. | 2. Bihar's demographic dividend is expected to peak around 2041. | 3. The elderly population (60+ years) in Bihar is expected to rise more sharply than in India. | Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: According to Bihar Economic Survey, 2024-25, Bihar’s population share in the 0–19 age group was about 49.4% in 2011, which is estimated to decline to about 30.1% by 2041. Therefore, a significant decline in the proportion of youth population up to 2041 is recorded. The population share of the working-age group (20–59 years) is estimated to increase from about 43.2% in 2011 to about 58.3% in 2041. The proportion of the elderly population is not expected to rise faster in Bihar (11.6%) than in India (15.9%); rather, it is expected to increase at a relatively slower pace.

subject: Bihar Special
question: According to PLFS 2023-24, which of the following statements best describe the nature of employment among women in Bihar?
option_a: Most women are employed in formal, regular wage jobs.
option_b: The majority of women are self-employed, often serving as helpers in household enterprises.
option_c: Majority of women were engaged in secondary sector.
option_d: More than one of the above
answer_text: The majority of women are self-employed, often serving as helpers in household enterprises.
explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) classifies employment into three major categories—self-employed, regular wage/ salaried, and casual labour. Analyses based on PLFS 2023–24 indicate that the largest share of working women in Bihar falls under the self-employed category. On the basis of PLFS 2023–24, under the Current Weekly Status (CWS), 83.7 percent of total female workers in Bihar are self-employed, 10.8 percent are casual labour, and only 5.5 percent are regular wage/salaried. Out of these 83.7 percent self-employed female workers, 39.8 percent are engaged as helpers in household enterprises. Note—The category of self-employed workers also includes those workers who had work in household enterprises but could not work due to illness or some other reason.

subject: Polity
question: The power to recruit the Secretarial staff of the House of the People is vested in:
option_d: President after consultation with the Speaker of the House of the people
answer_text: President after consultation with the Speaker of the House of the people
explanation: At the administrative level, the authority to issue appointment orders for the Lok Sabha Secretariat staff lies with the Speaker (Speaker of the Lok Sabha), while the constitutional rule-making power for this entire framework, under Article 98(3), lies with the President, who, after consultation with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, makes rules for regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of the Lok Sabha Secretariat staff. If it is viewed purely as “who issues the individual appointment orders”, then under the above constitutional provision, the appointing authority is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as per Rule 6 of the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, which are made by the President after consultation with the Speaker. Hence, the correct answer should be “Speaker of the Lok Sabha”, but it has not been given separately among the options.

subject: Polity
question: Attorney General of India:
option_a: Is not entitled of audience except the Supreme Court
option_b: He gives advice to the President on legal matters
option_c: Cannot participate in the proceedings in the House of Parliament
option_d: Is a whole time counsel for the government
answer_text: He gives advice to the President on legal matters
explanation: Article 76 defines the Attorney General (AG) as the highest law officer in the country. Their primary duty is to advise the Government of India (via the President) on legal issues. The Attorney General (AG) of India has the right to take part in the proceedings of the Parliament of India even thoughheis not amember of anyhouse.Heis the central chief legal advisor and primarily a lawyer in the supreme court of India. AG is appointed by the president under article 76 (1) and heis apart oftheunionexecutive. He is the highest law officer in the country.He must be a person qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court. The term ofhis office is notfixed by the constitution and hence he holds office at the pleasure of the president. According to Article 165 of the Indian constitution, the Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be Advocate-General for the State.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following subjects belonging to different lists of the constitution of India. Which of the following subjects belong to concurrent list? 1) Protection of wildlife 2) Income on Agriculture 3) Tax on Electricity 4) Price control
explanation: In the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, legislative subjects are divided into three lists—Union List (List I), State List (List II) and Concurrent List (List III). On subjects included in the Concurrent List, both Parliament and the State Legislatures can make laws; however, if there is a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by Parliament prevails. • Protection of wild animals and birds—Concurrent List, Entry 17B. • Tax on agricultural income—State List, Entry 46. • Tax on the electricity consumption or sale —State List, Entry 53. • Price control—Concurrent List, Entry 34. Therefore, as per the options, only (1) protection of wildlife and (4) price control come under the Concurrent List.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following Directive Principles do not follow Gandhian Principles? | 1. Organization of Village Panchayats | 2. Common Civil Code | 3. Promotion of cottage industry in rural areas | 4. Right to work
explanation: Statement 1 (Organisation of village panchayats) and 3 (promotion of cottage industries in rural areas) are in accordance with Gandhian principles, whereas statement 2 (Common Civil Code) and 4 (right to work) fall under other categories (liberal–intellectual and socialist) of Directive Principles, not Gandhian. Therefore, the Directive Principles not in accordance with Gandhian principles are 2 and 4.

subject: Polity
question: Which pair is not correctly matched?
option_a: Allocation of seats in the council of state - 4th schedule
explanation: Provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes are in the Fifth Schedule, not the Sixth. The Sixth Schedule relates to the administration of tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, not to Scheduled Areas in general.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements about Central Government: | 1. Ministries and Departments are formed by the Prime Minister with consultation of the Cabinet Secretary. | 2. Every Minister is allocated a Ministry by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. | Out of these:
explanation: Under Article 77(3), the President makes rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for the allocation of that business among ministers. Accordingly, the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 were made, which list the ministries/ departments and their subjects. New ministries/departments are created or reorganised by amending these rules through presidential amendments. As per these rules, the President allocates portfolios among ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

subject: Polity
question: What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature?
option_a: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English.
option_b: Advocate General has right to vote
option_c: It can discuss the conduct of any judge of the High Court also
option_d: Validity of proceedings shall be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity
answer_text: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English.
explanation: Article 210(1) of the Indian Constitution provides that business in the State Legislature shall be transacted in the official language(s) of the State, or in Hindi, or in English. Hence, statement (b) is true. Under Article 177, the Advocate-General may take part in the proceedings of the State Legislature, but he does not have the right to vote. Under Article 211, the State Legislature cannot discuss the conduct of a Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties. Under Article 212(1), the validity of proceedings in the State Legislature cannot be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

subject: Polity
question: The Constitution of India provides for reasonable restrictions on Fundamental Rights, but reasonableness must keep in mind that: | 1. The interest of the general public is safeguarded | 2. Prevailing social value and also social needs are not barred | 3. Directive Principles can be bypassed | 4. Collective good is not greater | Out of these:
explanation: Under Article 19, the freedoms granted (speech, expression, forming associations, free movement, etc.) may be subjected by the State, through law, to reasonable restrictions. From Article 19(2) to Article 19(6), it is provided that such limitations can be imposed only for certain specified purposes—such as the sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, protection of the interests of the general public, protection of the interests of Scheduled Tribes, and professional/technical schemes, etc.—or in relation to contempt of court, defamation, or incitement to an offence. Therefore, only statements 1 and 2 conform to the constitutional and judicial tests of reasonable restriction, while statements 3 and 4 are both incorrect.

subject: Polity
question: Who among the following determines the qualification which shall be requisite for appointment as member of the finance commission?
explanation: Article 280(2) of the Constitution of India clearly provides that the required qualifications for the members of the Finance Commission and the manner of their selection may be determined by Parliament by making a law.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements: | 1. The summoning of the House means convocation. | 2. Prorogation ends a session. | 3. Dissolution terminates a House. | 4. Prorogation of a session can be effected by the leader of the House alone. | Out of these, which is not true?
explanation: This question relates to the major procedures of the Indian Parliament/Legislature—Summoning, Adjournment, Prorogation, and Dissolution. Adjournment is done by the Presiding Officer/Speaker/Chairman (or the person acting as such), whereas prorogation is done by the President/Governor. Also, by adjournment, the House is adjourned for a definite or indefinite period; it does not end the session, i. e., it does not amount to prorogation. In fact, prorogation ends a session. Note: In the statement (4) Prorogation of a session can be effected by the leader of the House alone is incorrect. So answer is option (d).

subject: Polity
question: Who is empowered to review financial position of the Panchayats?
option_d: Finance Commission constituted by the Governor
answer_text: Finance Commission constituted by the Governor
explanation: Part IX of the Constitution contains provisions relating to Panchayats. According to Article 243-I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission, which is specifically authorized to review the financial position of Panchayats and to give recommendations to the Governor. This Commission also reviews the financial position of the municipalities of the State under Article 243-Y.

subject: Economics
question: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Scheme announced by the Government helps in: | 1. Enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities and exports across the industries. | 2. Incentivizing foreign investments for domestic production. | Out of these:
explanation: The declared objective of Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan is to increase domestic manufacturing capacity and develop India as a global supply chain and export hub. This campaign is not against foreign investment; rather, by liberalising the FDI policy in specific sectors, it encourages setting up production facilities in India itself (especially in defence and other manufacturing sectors).

subject: Polity
question: What is the main purpose of Panchayati Raj?
option_d: To enable people to participate in development administration
answer_text: To enable people to participate in development administration
explanation: In the Indian context, the basic objective of the Panchayati Raj system is “democratic decentralization with people’s participation.” That is, by taking the process of governance and development down to the village level, to make common people direct participants in decision-making and in the implementation of development programmes.

subject: Polity
question: What is true about Censure Motion?
option_a: It is not different from No-confidence motion
option_b: It is different from the No-confidence motion
option_c: It is not mandatory to mention the reasons in this motion
option_d: Permission of the House is not essential to present it
answer_text: Officially Deleted in BPSC Final Answer Key
explanation: [Officially Deleted in BPSC 71st Final Answer Key] Conceptually, a Censure Motion differs from a No-Confidence Motion (it requires stating specific reasons for adoption, can be moved against an individual minister or group of ministers, and need not cause resignation of the Council of Ministers), while leave/permission of the House is required. BPSC deleted Q.69 in the Final Answer Key.

subject: Polity
question: Which one of the following subjects fall within the jurisdiction of both High Court and Supreme Court?
option_d: Protection from the violation of the constitution
explanation: The protection of fundamental rights falls within thejurisdiction of both the High Courtandthe Supreme Court. To effectively protect these rights, both courts possess the power to review and invalidate any government action or law that violates them. The concept of "Judicial Review"is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution;this sharedpower is derivedfrom several articles: Article 13:Declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall be void. Supreme Court: Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can be approached for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It can also review the constitutionality of any law under Articles 131-136. High Courts:Under Article 226,High Courts have the power to issue writs for the enforcement Their power of judicial review is actually broader in scope than that of the Supreme Court because of the phrase “any other purpose."

subject: Modern History
question: Which Indian leader for the first time used the 'safety-valve theory' to attack the Moderates in the Congress?
explanation: For the first time, the extremist leader Lala Lajpat Rai, in his book Young India published in 1916, used this theory to accuse the moderate leaders of the Congress of running an organisation which the British rulers were using like a “safety-valve”.

subject: Modern History
question: At which Viceroy was a bomb thrown on the occasion of his state entry into Delhi?
explanation: In 1911, the British government announced shifting India’s capital from Calcutta to Delhi. After this, on 23 December, 1912, a grand state entry procession of Viceroy Lord Hardinge II was taken out in the new capital, Delhi. On this occasion, in the Chandni Chowk area of Delhi, revolutionaries threw a bomb at the Viceroy’s elephant howdah. In this attack, Lord Hardinge II was seriously injured and the mahout was killed. This attack was planned under the leadership of the revolutionary Rash Behari Bose.

subject: Modern History
question: Who got an opportunity to become Professor of Indian Philosophy in the University of California in 1911?
explanation: Har Dayal got an opportunity to become Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of California in 1911. He was a prominent Indian revolutionary and scholar, who played a crucial role in the Ghadar Movement for India's independence. His academic pursuits led him to this position in California, USA. BCWBits: Sohan Singh Bhakna was the founder of Ghadar Party. Shyamji Krishna Varma is known for founding India House in London.

subject: Modern History
question: Name the Principal of M.A.O. College, Aligarh, who encouraged Muslim Communalism in the last decades of the 19th Century?
explanation: M. A.O. College (Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College), Aligarh, was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. In the last decades of the 19th century, the ‘Muslim separatist’ tendencies that emerged here were encouraged by several persons, among whom the Principal of M. A.O. College, Aligarh, Theodore Beck, was prominent.

subject: Modern History
question: The Young India', a Nationalist paper, was started by
answer_text: Officially Deleted in BPSC Final Answer Key
explanation: [Officially Deleted in BPSC 71st Final Answer Key] 'Young India' was originally started as an English journal in 1916 in Bombay by the Home Rule League circle (Jamnadas Dwarkadas, Shankarlal Banker, and Indulal Yagnik, associated with Annie Besant) and was taken over and edited as a famous nationalist weekly by Mahatma Gandhi from October 1919 to 1931. Owing to this dual historical attribution between options (A) and (B), BPSC officially deleted Q.75 in the Final Answer Key.

subject: Modern History
question: Which Commission accentuated the discontent in all the political groups and parties for not associating any Indian member in it?
explanation: In 1927, the British government appointed a statutory commission to review the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919; it was called the Simon Commission. All seven members of this commission were British, and not even a single Indian representative from any Indian political party, group, community, or organization was included in it.

subject: Modern History
question: Who assumed the command of the Indian National Army and gave famous battle cry, 'Chalo Delhi'?
explanation: The initial formation of the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army—INA) took place during the Second World War with Japan’s support. In the early phase, Captain Mohan Singh and Ras Bihari Bose played an important role in its organisation, but later its leadership came into the hands of Subhas Chandra Bose. He organised the Azad Hind Fauj and gave the famous slogan “Chalo Delhi”.

subject: Modern History
question: "We shall either free India or die in the attempt" — who said it?
explanation: This statement was made by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 on the occasion of the Quit India Movement. In the session of the All India Congress Committee at the Gowalia Tank ground in Bombay (now Mumbai)—later known as “August Kranti Maidan”—Gandhiji gave this message in the form of his famous slogan “Do or Die”. In his speech, he said that Indians must now resolve that either they will make India free, or they will sacrifice their lives in this effort.

subject: Modern History
question: Who raised the cry "Divide and Quit"?
explanation: The slogan “Divide and Quit” was raised by the Muslim League leader Muhammad Ali Jinnah during the Second World War, in 1943. Jinnah and the Muslim League demanded that the British should first divide India into two parts—Hindustan and Pakistan—and then quit India. This idea was expressed in the form of the political slogan “Divide and Quit”.

subject: Modern History
question: Which Act provided for the partition of India into two new dominions - India and Pakistan?
explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, formally approved the partition of British India and provided the legal basis for the creation of two new independent dominions/states—India and Pakistan. This Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947, and it provided that from 15 August 1947 the two independent dominions/states India and Pakistan would come into existence.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Which Congress leader visited Bihar in 1918 in order to strengthen the activities of Home Rule League?
explanation: Annie Besant visited Bihar (Patna) twice in 1918; on 18 April, 1918 to strengthen the activities of the Home Rule League, and on 25 July, 1918 to understand the views of the Home Rulers. During these visits, she held meetings, increased contact with local workers, and strengthened the League’s organisational base.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Champaran Agrarian Committee was appointed in agreement between:
option_b: Indian Government and Raj Kumar Shukla
option_d: Indian Government and Anugraha Narayan Singh
explanation: During the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917, to inquire into the complaints of farmers suffering under the Tinkathia system of indigo cultivation, the colonial provincial government of Bihar and Orissa constituted a formal inquiry committee, commonly known as the Champaran Agrarian Committee or the Champaran Agrarian Inquiry Committee. The formation of this committee was the outcome of an agreement reached between Gandhiji and the then government.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who was the prominent leader of Kisan Sabha movement in Bihar?
explanation: With the objective of organizing farmers in Bihar and resolving their problems, the Bihar Provincial (Provincial) Kisan Sabha was established in November 1929 on the occasion of the Sonpur Fair. Swami Sahajanand was its first president. Its associates included Sahajanand Saraswati, Yadunandan (Jadunandan) Sharma, left-wing leader Karyanand Sharma, and other prominent personalities.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who was murdered while hoisting the national flag under the area of Bikram Police Station?
explanation: Under the Bikram Police Station, while hoisting the national flag, Rang Nath Sharma alias Raghunath Sharma was shot dead by the police on 17 August, 1942.

subject: Bihar Special
question: Who became Chief Minister of Bihar in March 1939?
explanation: Shri Krishna Singh remained the Premier (provincial head of government) of Bihar continuously from 20 July 1937 to 31 October 1939. March 1939 falls within this period; therefore, the head of government of Bihar at that time (in today’s terms, the Chief Minister) was Shri Krishna Singh. However, since the question uses the term “Chief Minister” instead of “Premier”, the Bihar Public Service Commission gave option (d) as the answer.

subject: Ancient History
question: Match List I with List II. | List-I (Places in Ancient India) | List-II (Presently in which State) | a. Karmasuvarna 1. Maharashtra | b. Pragjyotish 2. Gujarat | c. Girnar 3. West Bengal | d. Pratishthan 4. Assam
explanation: Archaeological and historical accounts describe Karnasuvarna as an ancient city, believed to be located in present-day Murshidabad district, West Bengal. Ancient Sanskrit literature uses the names Pragjyotisha and Kamarupa to refer to ancient Assam and its surrounding region. Mount Girnar and its associated ancient religious and historical sites lie in the modern-day state of Gujarat. subject: Geography
question: Maginot Line exists between which countries?
explanation: The Maginot Line was a massive system of fortifications constructed by France before the Second World War to prevent a possible German attack. It was mainly built along France’s eastern border facing Germany, and partly towards Luxembourg.

subject: Geography
question: Strait of Hormuz connects -

explanation: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman. It is an extremely important sea route that links the oil-rich region of West Asia with other parts of the world.

subject: Geography
question: Where is "Ground Zero"?
explanation: After the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, the buildings (including the Twin Towers) in the World Trade Center complex in New York City collapsed. This destroyed site is called Ground Zero. A rebuilt World Trade Center complex has now been developed at this site.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following Isthmuses has been known as the 'Devil's Neck'?
explanation: The Kra Isthmus is the narrowest part of the Malay Peninsula in Thailand.It has historically been referred to as the “Devil's Neck"(or sometimes the “Gorge of the Devil")due to several factors: Difficult Terrain:The areawas notoriouslydifficult to navigate and traverse in the past due to dense tropical jungles, rugged terrain, and the prevalence of diseases. ·Strategic Narrowness: Much like a “bottleneck,” this narrow strip of land separates the Gulf of Thailand (Pacific Ocean)from the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean). The Kra Canal Project: For centuries, engineers have proposed cutting a canal through this “neck" to bypass the long journey through the Strait of Malacca, a project often met with immense logistical and political "hellish" challenges. explanation: A Geographical Indication (GI) tag is given to a product whose name or sign links it to a specific geographical region, and it certifies that its distinctive quality, reputation, or other characteristics are associated with that region. explanation: Kanha National Park, also known as Kanha Tiger Reserve, is thelargest national park in Central India. ·Location: It is situated in the Maikalrange ofthe Satpuras inthe Mandla and Balaghat districts of Madhya Pradesh. question: We apply a force of 200 Newtons on a wooden Box and push it on the floor at constant velocity. The marginal friction force will be:
explanation: Constant velocity means that the rate of change of velocity, i. e., acceleration, is zero. Applied forward force = 200 N 2. Backward kinetic frictional force (limiting frictional force exerted by the floor on the wooden box) Since the net force is zero; hence kinetic frictional force = 200 N. Therefore, in this situation, the backward frictional force (limiting frictional force) acting on the box is 200 N, equal to the applied force but in the opposite direction.

question: A truck starts from rest down a hill with a constant acceleration. It achieves 400 meters in 20 seconds. If the weight of the truck is 7 tons then what will be the force acting on it?

subject: Physics
question: The potential energy of a freely falling body continuously decreases.
option_a: The principle of conservation of energy is violated
option_b: The principle of conservation of energy is not violated
answer_text: The principle of conservation of energy is not violated
explanation: Assuming air resistance is negligible, only gravitational force does work on a freely falling body. The decrease in potential energy does not violate the law of conservation of energy; it is a normal example of conversion of energy from one form (potential energy) to another form (kinetic energy). Hence, statement of option (b) is correct. Similarly, gravitational force is a conservative force. When the body moves downward (in the direction of gravity), the decrease in potential energy and increase in kinetic energy occurs exactly as expected by gravitational theory. There is no violation of the gravitational force or law of gravitation. Hence, statement of option (d) is also correct. The Bihar Public Service Commission has given option (b) as correct answer for this question.

subject: Physics
question: A pair of Oxen exerts a force of 140 newton while ploughing the field. The field ploughed is 15 meter long. The work done in ploughing the length of the field is:
explanation: 1 Joule is the amount of work done when a force of one Newton displaces a body by one meter in the direction of the force applied. Therefore, Work done = Force x Displacement Given, Force = 140 N, displacement = 15 meter So, Work done =140 N x 15 m =2100 Joule Hence, the work done in ploughing the field is 2100 Joule. BCW Bits: ·The general formula for work is W=F x d × cos 0, where 0 is the angle between the force and displacement. Here, since the oxen pull horizontally along the direction of motion (0 = 0°, cos 0° = 1), the formula simplifies to W =Fxd.

question: The focal distance of a plane mirror is:
explanation: The focal length (focal distance)is defined as the distance where parallel incident rays converge or appear to converge. For a plane mirror, because the reflected rays are parallel, they only meet at an infinite distance. Therefore, the focal distance of a plane mirror is at infinity. BCW Bits: A plane mirror is a flat reflective surface that does not converge or diverge light rays in the same way curved mirrors do. Thus,a plane mirror can be considered a part of a sphere with an infinite radius of curvature.

subject: Physics
question: What is the device to protect equipments from the electric shock?
explanation: A fuse is an essential electrical safety device designed to protect appliances and circuits from damage caused by excessive current. It operates on the principle of the heating effect of electric current, where the heat generated in a conductor is proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time of flow (expressed by the relationship H=IRt). A fuse wire is engineered with a low melting point and high resistivity, commonly made from an alloy of tin and lead. When an abnormally high current fows through the circuit due to overloading or a short circuit, the wire rapidly heats up, reaches its melting point, and breaks. This action creates an open circuit, instantly interrupting theelectricalflow and shielding connected equipment from severe damage or fire hazards. In modernelectricallayouts,Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) are preferred over traditional fuses because they automatically switch off (trip) during faults and can be easilyresetwithout thehassleofreplacing awire. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy to produce power, a motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy to drive machinery, and a current controller simplyregulates currentflow to a steady level rather than cutting off the circuit during a dangerous power spike. BCW Bits: ·It is worth noting that a fuse protects equipment from damage due to excess current, it does not protect humans from electric shock directly. For personal shock protection, ELCB (Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker)or RCD(Residual Current Device) are used, which detect leakage current and trip the circuit within milliseconds.

It is commonly used in safety signs, watches, and paints due to its ability to absorb light and emit a long-lasting, bright glow for up to 12 hours.

explanation: Smart film or switchable smart film is generally a PDLC (Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal) film. For the transparent conductive layer of smart film, indium tin oxide (ITO)-coated PET or glass is commonly used. explanation: Carcinoma is a cancer that arises from epithelial tissue (the lining of the skin or internal organs). In the treatment of carcinoma and many other solid tumors, platinum-based compounds (mainly cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin) are widely used chemotherapy drugs.

explanation: Common oral contraceptive pills and emergency contraceptive pills are mainly based on a synthetic progestogen; the most commonly used compound is levonorgestrel.

question: Why oil is not stored in galvanized iron pot?
explanation: Galvanized iron is iron coated with a layer of zinc (Zn) to protect it from rusting. The zinc layer reacts with free fatty acids and moisture present in oil and forms toxic zinc compounds. Zinc salts and metal ions increase the rate of oxidation (rancidity) of oil, thereby reducing its quality. Due to these reactions, the protective zinc layer gradually gets corroded, and the iron underneath comes in contact with moisture and oxygen; as a result, corrosion and rust are clearly observed. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

question: Which compound is used for increase of octane rating?
explanation: Octane rating is a measure of petrol’s ability (quality) to burn in a controlled manner during compression without causing engine knocking. Tetraethyl lead was used to increase the octane rating of petrol; it reduced engine knock, and the engine could run more smoothly at higher compression. explanation: A parasite requires the host cell’s metabolic energy and the host’s protein-synthesis system for replication, and this causes harm to the host cell. Therefore, such a biological relationship is called parasitism. The Herpes simplex virus lives inside human cells and is completely dependent on them for nutrition and replication, and it harms humans; hence, the “interaction” (biological relationship) between the two is correctly termed parasitism, which is expressed by option (a). question: The biological membranes are composed of:
option_a: Lipids and proteins in varying combinations which are specific to each species, cell type and organelle
answer_text: Lipids and proteins in varying combinations which are specific to each species, cell type and organelle
explanation: Biological membranes are mainly made of various combinations of lipids and proteins, which are specific to a species, cell type, and organ. According to the modern fluid mosaic model, the basic framework of the membrane is a phospholipid bilayer (lipid bilayer), in which different types of proteins are found floating or embedded.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a non-sense codon?
explanation: In Genetics, a three-nucleotide sequence of mRNA is called a codon. Codons are of two types— Sense codons: These are codons for amino acids and are responsible for protein formation. Their total number is 61. Nonsense (stop) codons: These indicate the termination of protein synthesis. In the standard genetic code, three major stop (nonsense) codons are accepted. These give the termination signal for protein synthesis— UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), and UGA (opal) Therefore, among the given options, only UAA is a nonsense (stop) codon. The remaining are sense codons.

question: The species which are in danger of extinction are known as?
explanation: According to the IUCN Red List, Endangered species face a very high risk of extinction in the wild.Rare species have small, localized, or scattered populations that are naturally vulnerable but not yet endangered. Vulnerable indicates a high risk of extinction(one step below endangered), while Extinct means no living individuals remain.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
explanation: In India, mainly three major crop seasons are considered- Kharif, Rabi and Zaid. Barley, gram and wheat- all three are Rabi crops. Sugarcane is technically an annual/longduration cash crop. Compared to Rabi crops (barley, gram, wheat), sugarcane is placed more on the Kharif side because it requires higher temperature and relatively more water, and in the crop-classification of many states it is linked with the Kharif/monsoon-based season.

subject: Biology
question: Xylem in plants is responsible for following function:
option_a: Transport of water and dissolved minerals
option_c: Transport of oxygen and other gases
answer_text: Transport of water and dissolved minerals
explanation: Xylem is one of the vascular (conducting) tissues of vascular plants. Its main function is to carry the water and dissolved mineral salts absorbed by the roots to the stem, leaves, and other parts of the plant. This transport generally occurs from bottom to top (from root to leaf), so it is considered unidirectional transport.

question: Who was first to use the characteristics of vascular tissues in the classification of plants?
option_d: More than one of the above
explanation: A. P. de Candolle (Augustin Pyramus de Candolle) was a Swiss botanist, who coined the word “taxonomy” for the first time and developed a natural system of plant classification. The systematic use of characteristics of vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) in plant classification was first done by A. P. de Candolle.

question: Ozone day is celebrated on:
explanation: World Ozone Day, or the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer, is observed every year on 16 September. Notably, the Montreal Protocol for the protection of the ozone layer came into effect from 16 September 1987. It is noteworthy that in 1994, the United Nations General Assembly announced the observance of this day.

subject: Biology
question: In mycorrhizal association, the advantage of plant is:
option_d: Increased mineral absorption and diseases protection
answer_text: Increased mineral absorption and diseases protection
explanation: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association formed between certain fungi and the roots of higher plants. In this association, the plant especially benefits through increased absorption of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other micronutrients. Plants with mycorrhiza also get protection from root-borne diseases and some harmful soil microorganisms.
